articleBody:
When I moved from the San Francisco Bay Area to a small, rural town in Vermont, I wanted to find a way to contribute to the local community. Knowing there was a significant senior population here, I reached out to the town librarian with hopes of helping elders share their stories.

The local historical society took interest in this idea, which led to an exhibit at the 159-year-old Tunbridge World’s Fair, and a book series entitled *Folk Life: Tunbridge Oral Histories*. The first two print runs sold out. The second collection of stories has just been published, and people are already asking who will be featured in the third.

What is it about life stories that strikes such a universal chord? And why is it important—and even imperative—to share our stories with others? I interviewed oral historians, teachers, and a digital storyteller to discover more about why the age-old tradition of recording oral histories continues to make such a significant impact for individuals and communities.

## Fostering connections and reflection

Storytelling is, according to scientific research, a biological shortcut to human connection. [Uri Hasson](https://blog.ted.com/what-happens-in-the-brain-when-we-hear-stories-uri-hasson-at-ted2016/) and fellow researchers at Princeton University discovered that the brains of the storyteller and listener physically sync up while a story is being told, promoting social connection, trust, and empathy.

The more emotionally affecting the story is, the stronger this connection becomes. As emotions and tension rise, hormones are released, including oxytocin, the “bonding hormone”; dopamine, which sharpens focus; and cortisol, which promotes attention and alertness as conflicts in the story arise. These hormonal responses enhance both the listener’s memory and connection to the storyteller.

For Erin Barnaby, a digital storyteller and 11th-generation Tunbridge native, oral histories create a connection not only to people, but also time and place. “My dad recently sold his house to my uncle, a house that he built on land that my grandfather had given to him. I love to hear him tell stories about the shifting of the land, from sheep farms to dairy farms and the shift from open pastures to forests.”

Even when the subject matter might not be instantly relatable, the process of listening to another’s stories still creates a profound interpersonal connection. Esther Ehrlich, who worked at [UC Berkeley’s Oral History Center](https://www.lib.berkeley.edu/visit/bancroft/oral-history-center) for six years before launching an oral history business of her own, experienced this sense of connection firsthand:

> I was assigned an interview with a former medical malpractice insurance guy, which initially didn’t interest me at all. And then lo and behold, after interviewing this man, I found him absolutely fascinating. What I came to discover was that by the time we were done, or even partway in, I came to love every single person I interviewed. I would feel connected to them and them to me.

## Providing unique perspectives

From that biological and psychological basis, oral histories make a critical social contribution.

According to the [Oral History Association](https://oralhistory.org/), “oral history is the oldest type of historical inquiry, stemming from the oral traditions of myriad cultures across the globe, predating even the written word.” These personal stories expand upon the narratives of history books, allowing people from varied walks of life to share their unfiltered experiences and perspectives. Indeed, many works by trained historians rely on oral histories.

The founders of [Voice of Witness](https://voiceofwitness.org/), a nonprofit dedicated to advancing human rights by amplifying unheard voices, believe that oral history “can democratize history, contribute to narrative change, and illuminate issues and events in a profoundly powerful way.” Enabling individuals to safely share their stories opens people’s minds to fresh perspectives and vantage points.

While oral histories are limited to an individuals’ memories and are by nature subjective, they remain incredibly valuable in their ability to paint a portrait of time and place. Plus, their narrative-driven format brings history to life in a more memorable way than date- and fact-focused textbooks.

Helen Marks, a former history teacher who has spoken to thousands of students about her experience as a hidden child in Belgium during World War II, has observed that when a person shares their stories, it brings that part of history to life:

> I am among the few surviving hidden children who are willing and able to talk about their experiences in the Holocaust. Reading numbers on a page does not create the same impact as someone standing or sitting in front of you describing a moment that was frightening or was so foreign they didn’t know what to do.... I think that when you connect a face, no matter what the face looks like, you get a wholly different reaction than when you read a page full of facts.

## Leaving a legacy

Throughout the interviews I conducted for *Folk Life*, the importance of leaving a meaningful legacy was a common theme. “That’s the reason we share our stories,” says Marsha Higgins, a history teacher for nearly 40 years. “It makes us feel like we matter.”

Higgins taught students to create personal narratives from a young age. Decades later, former students still express their thanks for her guidance in teaching them the importance of recording their experiences.

“I encouraged students to write down things that happened to them. It’s helpful to know at the time, you’re creating chapters in your life, that your story is just as interesting as anybody else’s.”

Like Marks, Higgins grew up around immigrants from Europe. “And they all had stories,” she says. “Whenever we got together, somebody would tell me a story. How do you make conversation without one? It’s just so much a part of who we are.”

“I think everyone wants to know that they have made a positive difference,” says Marks. “That they did some good, that their being here wasn’t just a fleeting moment of nothingness, but that they contributed something. They reacted to something. They gave something. So when you tell stories, that’s where you learn about people and what they value.”

## Gaining newfound awareness

Neal Allen, a coach and author (most recently of *Good Writing: 36 Ways to Improve Your Sentences* with his wife Anne Lamott), spent several years as a hospice volunteer. During that time, he helped a number of people share and record their stories.

“Every week I had one or two clients who were dying, and I spent time fluffing their pillows, listening to their stories and how they approach death. The funny thing is we were always asked, ‘Oh, isn’t that hard?’ It was quite the opposite. It was really quite extraordinary.”

A seasoned journalist, Allen knew how to ask evocative questions. “Oddball memories were coming up that hadn’t come up in 50 years maybe,” he says, which led to more and more stories. “My subjects would get really involved in it. To finish their story, it would take eight to 12 hours, sometimes up to 40 hours.”

Allen wrote a biography about his father, which proved to be a learning opportunity for both him and his brothers:

> Once [the book] was bound and we read it all the way through, we had the same reaction, ‘Oh, I didn’t know he had done this. Oh, I didn’t know he had done this. Oh, did you know about that?’ Our second reaction was, ‘We’re not in it,’ and burst out laughing. It was easy to laugh about because he never, ever gave us any sign that he disapproved of us in any fundamental way.

For older adults, sharing stories not only connects them with family, each other, and audiences, it also exercises the brain and fosters a sense of well-being. Story sharing activates memory networks while encouraging reflection on past experiences.

[Reminiscence therapy](https://www.nature.com/nature-index/topics/l4/reminiscence-therapy-for-enhancing-mental-health-in-older-adults), a structured method of helping individuals recall, organize, and share life stories, has proven helpful in elevating people’s moods, enhancing their self-esteem, resolving conflict, and promoting meaning. This mode of therapy is becoming increasingly popular as a way to support seniors facing cognitive decline as well as mental health challenges.

## Storytelling brings us together

Ehrlich notes that more than ever, hearing or reading about others’ stories is a powerful tool for building bridges, especially in this divisive climate.

“We have so much more in common than not,” she says, noting that “there’s a desperate need to understand each other better. Oral history is perhaps a tool for seeing beyond our rigid ideas of who people are and breaking through into a fuller understanding.”

“What always astonished the subject of the memoirs was how many people they had touched,” says Allen. “I think we touch a far greater number of people than we can hold or remember at any one time.”

In this way, sharing stories reminds us that our interactions have more of an impact than we realize, not only in our close-knit circles, but also at work, at school, and even in everyday exchanges.

What sharing our stories boils down to, Ehrlich believes, is that it’s a fundamental human instinct:

> How do we live a life? How do we deal with joy and difficulty and disappointment and pleasure? How do we make choices? What do we have control over? What don’t we have control over? Oral histories, at their most basic, include all the stuff that makes us people, including our desire to be seen, heard, and understood. And everybody’s stories matter.

title: XRecer XR1: Modeling-Newcomer mit Touchscreen, NAM-A2-Unterstützung und jeder Menge Leistung
subtitle: Mit dem XRecer XR1 tritt ein neuer Modeling-Verstärker und Multieffekt auf den Markt, der vorab bereits einige Vorschusslorbeeren einheimst.
feedText:

articleBody:
**Mit dem XRecer XR1 tritt ein neuer Modeling-Verstärker und Multieffekt auf den Markt, der vorab bereits einige Vorschusslorbeeren einheimst. Die Ankündigung deutet auf ein leistungsstarkes und flexibles System hin und hört sich entsprechend vielversprechend an. Nun ist der Modeler des neuen chinesischen Herstellers vorbestellbar. Kommt hier die nächste Konkurrenz für Neural DSP und Line 6?**

## Üppige Ausstattung mit Octa-Core-Prozessor und 10-Zoll-Touchscreen

Dank leistungsstarker Prozessoren und der Unterstützung des NAM-A2-Formats verschwimmen die Grenzen zwischen den etablierten Platzhirschen von Fractal Audio, Kemper, Line 6, Neural DSP und Fender sowie der günstigeren Konkurrenz. Unter den zahlreichen neuen Produkten sticht insbesondere der XRecer XR1 hervor, der im bühnentauglichen Pedalboard-Format mit zwölf Fußschaltern und einem 10-Zoll-Touchscreen direkt klotzt statt zu kleckern. Angetrieben wird das System von einer leistungsstarken Octa-Core-CPU, ergänzt durch GPU und Neural Processing Unit (NPU). Hinzu kommt ein integriertes 16×16-USB-Audio-Interface.

Die Hersteller-Webseite zeigt eine Bedienoberfläche mit vier parallelen Signalwegen und jeweils acht Slots, die Platz für jede Menge Amps und Effekte bieten. Auch die Rückseite ist beeindruckend ausgestattet: Neben vier Instrumenteneingängen und einem Mikrofoneingang stehen symmetrische XLR- und Klinkenausgänge, zwei Expression-Pedal-Anschlüsse, zwei Effektschleifen sowie MIDI zur Verfügung. Ein Looper ist ebenfalls integriert.

## Modeling, Effekte und NAM-A2-Kompatibilität inklusive TONE3000-Anbindung

Die Kompatibilität zum Open-Source-Format NAM dürfte für etliche Musiker interessant sein, steht hier doch ein großer Fundus fertig erfasster Verstärker und anderer Sounds zur Verfügung. Der XR1 unterstützt neben älteren NAM-A1-Modellen auch NAM A2 Full und A2 Lite. Besonders interessant ist die direkte Integration der Tone-Library von TONE3000: Über das WLAN des Geräts lassen sich passende Profile durchsuchen und herunterladen, ohne dafür einen Computer bemühen zu müssen.

Dazu kommt das proprietäre Capture-Format CapX, mit dem sich eigene Verstärker und Pedale erfassen lassen. Außerdem bietet der XR1 zahlreiche Effekte und die Möglichkeit, Impulsantworten von Drittanbietern zu laden. Die integrierten Amp- und Effektmodelle ergänzen das Angebot. Laut Hersteller umfasst die Ausstattung unter anderem 50 Amp-Modelle, 13 Cabinet-Modelle und 111 Effektmodelle. Üppige Rigs und komplexe Effektkombinationen scheinen damit möglich. Dank der vier parallelen Signalwege lassen sich zudem mehrere Signalquellen innerhalb eines Presets bearbeiten.

## Preis und Verfügbarkeit

Mit dem XR1 dürfte der neue chinesische Hersteller XRecer ein heißes Eisen im Feuer haben. Nun darf man auf die klangliche Performance gespannt sein. Der XRecer XR1 lässt sich ab sofort im Musikhaus Thomann zu einem knackigen Preis von 1.399 Euro vorbestellen. Die Lieferzeit soll bei sechs bis acht Wochen liegen – etwas Geduld muss man also mitbringen.

Weitere Informationen unter: [https://www.xrecer.com/products/xr1](https://www.xrecer.com/products/xr1)

articleBody:
Last week, the AI company Anthropic went public in what became the largest IPO in American history. Given my sustained criticism of Anthropic’s beliefs and actions, many people have asked me for my opinion on this event.

The good news for the curious among you is that I captured my thoughts in an op-ed for *The New York Times*, which they published Thursday, the same day that Anthropic went public. It was titled “[Don’t Play Anthropic’s Game](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/19/opinion/anthropic-ipo-ai-regulation.html),” and it opens as follows:

“By the close of the stock market today, Anthropic will have become a central pillar of the American economy. This is deeply concerning to me, because it’s unclear how many of the retail and institutional investors handing over their money to Anthropic realize that they are, in some sense, funding a doomsday cult that also happens to build enterprise software.”

My use of “doomsday cult” isn’t facetious; it underscores a critical reality. As many have reported ([including myself](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/05/opinion/ai-silicon-valley.html)), the leaders of Anthropic have long believed that AI is destined to transform the human species, either delivering a utopia or killing us all. They see themselves, with their highly rational minds, trained on long hours during the 2000s debating these issues on blogs like *Less Wrong* and *Overcoming Bias*, as the select few who must rise up to guide humanity through this next evolution.

This may sound like hyperbole, but it’s not. [It’s exactly what they believe](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jt508VjX2H8).

Some ask, “Why is this a problem? If any company is going to advance AI, shouldn’t it be one that cares about bad outcomes?”

As I elaborate in my op-ed, the situation is not so simple. Anthropic’s belief that transformational AI is imminent has made it reckless. Anthropic now releases models faster than they can build safeguards because they believe the fate of the human race depends on getting to superintelligent AI first. (Case in point: earlier this year, they announced they were relaxing rules that required them to slow down development if models became hard to control. Their reason? If they applied such rules “unilaterally,” other – presumably less righteous – parties might get ahead of them in the race.)

Indeed, Anthropic stated a key rationale for their IPO is to raise the money needed to accelerate investments in so-called “recursive self-improvement,” where AI systems upgrade themselves. This is, of course, a terrible idea, as it creates models that are even less safe and harder to understand. Anthropic acknowledged these risks in its S-1 filing, but sees no alternative if they’re to continue as humanity’s shepherd through this revolution.

It’s unclear to what degree they even care about profits or building a durable business. As I summarize in my op-ed:

“It’s a business plan that starts with a lot of red ink and then abruptly ends with superintelligence arriving and rendering money superfluous.”

To be clear: generative AI is an incredibly important technological revolution. It brings with it great promises and real risks. But the right way to navigate these innovations can’t possibly be to let a small number of people in Silicon Valley, who have been worshipping AI as a millenarian agent since well before LLMs entered the scene, gather as much money as possible to fund their self-proclaimed role as prophets who will lead the rest of us to their idiosyncratic vision of a better future.

#### In Other News

For more on the question of whether Amodei and company are right in their beliefs that we’re on a trajectory toward superintelligence, check out [my recent technical article](https://spectrum.ieee.org/ai-superintelligence-debate) for the *IEEE Spectrum*, which lays out an engineering case against the feasibility of AI superintelligence. (You should also consider signing up for the Spectrum’s always insightful [AI Alert newsletter](https://spectrum.ieee.org/ai-alert-signup).)

articleBody:
# Neuer Kopfhörer von HEDD - der HEDDphone DX ist da!

## HEDD HEDDphone DX Kopfhörer

## Verbesserter Kopfhörer - auch Upgrade-Kit erhältlich!

HEDD HEDDphone DX Kopfhörer

HEDD Audio kündigt den HEDDphone DX an, einen neuen dynamischen und offenen Kopfhörer. Der DX baut auf dem D1 von HEDD auf, nutzt aber eine neue 50-mm-TPC-Membran (Thin-Ply Carbon Diaphragm) mit hoher Auslenkung, um laut Hersteller tiefe Bässe hinab bis 20 Hz bei vollem Pegel auszugeben. Darüber hinaus soll der HEDD HEDDphone DX eine verfeinerte Höhenwiedergabe und eine breite Stereobühne bieten.

## HEDD HEDDphone DX

Im Zentrum des neuen HEDDphone DX steht ein 50 mm-Treiber mit Thin-Ply-Carbon-Diaphragm-Technologie (TPCD). Die ultradünne, geschichtete Kohlefasermembran verbindet ein geringes Gewicht mit hoher Steifigkeit und zusammen mit einer präzisen Konstruktion soll diese schnelle, kontrollierte Bewegungen über den gesamten Frequenzbereich ermöglichen und dabei unerwünschte Resonanzen reduzieren. Laut HEDD ist eine detailreiche Wiedergabe mit minimalen Verzerrungen und einer differenzierten Darstellung das Ergebnis.

Neben den klanglichen Eigenschaften hat HEDD den Kopfhörer auch beim Thema Tragekomfort weiterentwickelt. Dafür wurde gemeinsam mit Capra Audio ein neuer Federkopfbügel hergestellt. So soll ein elastisches Neoprenband das Gewicht des Kopfhörers von 310 g gleichmäßig über den Kopf verteilen und so auch bei langen Hörsessions für einen stabilen, komfortablen Sitz sorgen.

Ein offener Kapselrücken und lasergravierte Details ergänzen das Design.

Zum Lieferumfang des HEDD HEDDphone DX gehört ein symmetrisches 2,2 m langes OCC-Kabel sowie ein Transportcase mit einer doppelter Schutzhülle.

Wie alle HEDDphone-Modelle wird auch der DX in Berlin montiert und geprüft. Sämtliche Komponenten sind austauschbar, zudem ist optional eine erweiterte 5 Jahres Garantie erhältlich.

Der Kopfhörer ist ab sofort zum Preis von 1.199,- Euro im Handel erhältlich.

Ab Ende Januar 2027 wird dann der aktualisierte D1 mit dem oben beschriebenen neuen Kopfband für 799,- Euro erhältlich sein. Das aktualisierte Modell ist 30 g leichter als der bisherige D1. Besitzer des D1 können sich dann das „Headband Upgrade Kit“ für 99,- Euro zulegen.

Sie sehen gerade einen Platzhalterinhalt von YouTube . Um auf den eigentlichen Inhalt zuzugreifen, klicken Sie auf die Schaltfläche unten. Bitte beachten Sie, dass dabei Daten an Drittanbieter weitergegeben werden.

Mehr Informationen Inhalt entsperren Erforderlichen Service akzeptieren und Inhalte entsperren

articleBody: Background: Generative AI (GenAI) tools are increasingly used for health information and emotional support, yet little is known about their use for mental health by university students, a population with high digital literacy and elevated mental health need. Objective: To estimate the prevalence of GenAI use for mental health support among respondents to a survey at a single UK university and to identify demographic and well-being characteristics associated with use. Methods: Cross-sectional online survey of students at a large UK university. The primary outcome was self-reported GenAI use for mental health support in the past 6 months. Well-being was assessed using the Short Warwick-Edinburgh Mental Wellbeing Scale. Associations were examined using multivariable modified Poisson regression to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios. Results: Of 22,207 students invited, 2020 responded (response rate 9.1%). Among respondents, 25.0% (n=503) reported GenAI use for mental health support in the past 6 months. The most common reasons were advice when emotionally distressed (n=380, 19.3%), insights into mental health (n=256, 12.7%), and using GenAI as a personal therapist or coach (n=173, 8.6%); 2.7% (n=54) reported using GenAI to seek support when experiencing thoughts of self-harm. Use was more common among students aged 26-29 years, those identifying as Asian, students reporting a declared disability, students enrolled in management programs, and those with lower well-being. Conclusions: Among respondents at a UK university, approximately one in four reported using GenAI for mental health support. Use was concentrated among students reporting poorer well-being and disability, suggesting that GenAI may function as an informal help-seeking pathway. Universities and health services should anticipate GenAI as a help-seeking pathway and ensure appropriate guidance, integration with existing services, and safeguards to support safe and equitable use.

title: learning to move is how we first construct ourselves, and then everything around us
subtitle: Sometime in the fifth century B.C., Greek sculptors worked out a way to put motion into something that could not move.

articleBody:
Sometime in the fifth century B.C., Greek sculptors worked out a way to put motion into something that could not move. Contrapposto, as Renaissance artists would later name it, describes a standing figure resting its weight on a single leg, allowing the hips, shoulders, and torso to tilt in opposing directions. Against the stiff, frontal poses of the Archaic statues that came before it, contrapposto introduced a frozen promise of movement.

In 1968, [Bruce Nauman](https://www.designboom.com/tag/bruce-nauman/) walked it. Hands clasped behind his neck, hips swaying, he carried the pose up and down a narrow wooden corridor in his studio. That single-channel video became the basis for a series he was still making half a century later, shown in 2021 at Punta della Dogana. What stayed with me was the scale: seven projections, each large enough to make a man in a T-shirt and jeans feel monumental, and the flesh-and-blood performers executing the exact instructions he had written at the end of the sixties.

Watching them inhabit those movements in the same room pulled Nauman’s interrogation of the body out of the abstract; you were no longer just observing a study of human nature from a distance, but suddenly conscious of your own weight and footing beside them. Curators Carlos Basualdo and Caroline Bourgeois described his original video as a confrontation with *‘the simple fact of learning to walk as our first real way of constructing ourselves.’* What is true of the body turns out to be true of almost everything built around it. We make ourselves by moving, and then we remake the world to suit the way we move.

Bruce Nauman, Contrapposto Studies III, 2015-2016 | via designboom’s article [↗ designboom.com](https://www.designboom.com/art/palazzo-grassi-bruce-nauman-archive-for-the-future-conversations-04-24-2021/)

Time itself was remade across entire countries to accommodate a new way of moving. Until the 1840s, every British town kept its own hours, read off its own sun: Oxford ran five minutes behind London, Carnforth eleven, Barrow nearly thirteen. Then the trains arrived, and the clocks had to agree. The Great Western Railway switched to ‘railway time’ in November 1840; the Railway Clearing House ordered Greenwich into every station in 1847; and by 1855, roughly 98 percent of British towns had surrendered their local noon. North America began coordinating its schedules only after two trains running on different clocks collided at Valley Falls in 1853, and it took another three decades to settle the matter nationally. Your phone tells the time it does because movement needed everyone to agree, and almost everything built since has been designed to take time out of the journey.

The shorter word for this is speed. French philosopher and urbanist Paul Virilio, who approached the subject through architecture, spent a career arguing that speed is a political arrangement rather than a technical fact. We live less in a democracy, he wrote, than in a dromocracy: the reign of speed. Yet if speed is a political decision, then pace is something that was decided, and anything that was decided can be decided differently. This chapter is an account of the people doing exactly that.

Airports and railway stations are being rebuilt as places with a reason to linger, reversing a century of infrastructure meant only to push crowds through. Inside the vehicle, the engine no longer dictates the form around it, turning the cabin into a room—an idea now spilling off the road into campers, floating homes, and habitats untethered from land altogether. Cities are reclaiming lanes from cars and handing them back to pedestrians; trains are running slowly on purpose again; transit is being drawn for bodies it was never meant to hold; and the corridors that highways once severed are being stitched back together for the wildlife that used them first.

illustration by [Philippos Avramides](https://www.behance.net/philavramides) © designboom

The promise in contrapposto is a step that never arrives. Nauman’s contribution was to finally take it, awkwardly, for an hour, discovering in the process a body and a room he had not quite met before. States of Motion looks into that same interval: the uneasy, productive space between deciding to move another way, figuring out how to do it, and experiencing what takes shape when we actually do.

articleBody:
# Cassiopeia Production Suite 1 Bundle

Reviews » Gear/Software » Cassiopeia Production Suite 1 Bundle Cassiopeia Production Suite 1 Bundle Share Facebook Twitter WhatsApp These four Kontakt instruments from Soundsphat deliver thousands of highly editable, release-ready presets. Let’s see what sample-based sound design has to offer your productions.

Software synthesizers completely revolutionized the way music was made, and the sound of almost every genre of music has changed as a result. But arguably at least as influential to the music we hear today were sample-based instruments, such as those made for NI’s Kontakt.

From meticulously recreated playable orchestras to special effects and sound design tools, everybody with a computer can produce more complex, modulatable tones in seconds than the entire BBC Radiophonic Workshop could manage in decades.

But with so many analogue-modelled soft synths on the market today, it feels like we rarely use sampled instruments for our core sounds. Which is where the Cassiopeia bundle of Kontakt instruments comes in.

Guided by Grammy-nominated Christian Beat Hirt, Soundsphat aims to deliver a definitive selection of production-ready presets, complete with performance and modulation options, and all of the envelope, filter, and effects controls you could desire.

## Production Suite 1 Overview

There are four instruments in the package: Cassiopeia, Landlord Stabs, Zerotone 6, and The Riga Piano. Each has its own sonic concept but all share a similar interface and layer-based approach to sound design, so we’ll devote most of this review to the headline instrument, Cassiopeia, then explain how the others each riff on this concept.

Cassiopeia is based around four sound layers. The first two play host to the core sound layers like multisampled analogue synth layers, custom wavetables, acoustic-instrument-sourced waveforms, and more. The second two are sound-design-focused layers, including everything from bird calls and bells to subs and metal clangs. You can even add your own layers.

In terms of content, the headline figures are pretty impressive: a 422 GB library size (compressed to around 350 GB on your drive) with 58,000 samples, 120 custom wavetables, and 3,922 multisampled patches.

The sound design is top-notch throughout and the biggest selling point of this package by far. You could absolutely make complete, great-sounding tracks with nothing more than the sounds on offer here. Every kind of patch is covered, from basses and leads to pads and effects. And they’re incredibly polished, rich, slathered in effects, and ready to use.

For all that variety, though, this collection does very much have a distinct vibe. And it’s aimed squarely at the dancefloor and energetic playlists, so if you don’t like those kinds of sounds, this probably won’t be your bag.

## Cassiopeia In Use

Once you’ve found your sounds there is a powerful range of editing options.

The main interface is fairly uncomplicated with an X-Y modulation matrix for simultaneous real-time modulation of multiple effects and some headline parameters such as pitch bend range, filter cutoff and resonance, tone, volume, and velocity sensitivity. Plus buttons to add/mute each of the four sound layers that make up a Cassiopeia patch.

There are then six editing pages. EDIT offers up various controls. For example, polyphony, portamento, and a chord maker feature. Then you can apply up to nine effects: Reverb/convolution, Room, Comp, Delay, EQ, Tape, Chorus, Flanger, and Phaser, with detailed controls for each.

Next comes ADSR, offering up assignable envelope control for volume, cutoff, and pitch of each individual layer. This is very welcome, but unfortunately brings us to the first of only two gripes about this synth. The way you assign the envelopes to the layers is really unintuitive, and hard to understand even after reading the manual. You use the same on/off button to assign a voice to an envelope group as you do to call up that voice’s individual envelope settings. It’s definitely worth revisiting in an update.

Speaking of which, the LFO page has the same sound-shaping benefits and confusing assignment system as ADSR.

Luckily the ARP window is not confusing at all, offering a powerful and intuitive step-sequence-style programmer and all of the swing and timing controls you’d hope for. There’s even a randomize function.

It’s no surprise, then, that some of the most satisfying patches in the whole instrument are found in the ARP preset category – there’s just something fundamentally usable about them, enhanced by the top-tier sound design of each patch. Just keep an eye on the timing as you’ll find most arp-based patches need between −5 and −20 ms of track delay to slot into a project.

The MIX window comes next, with level and pan controls for each of the four layers, plus individual per-layer controls for things like pitch (semitones and cents), high- and low-pass filters, and Body and Silk (for boosting or easing low-mid and high-mid frequencies, respectively).

The layer-based architecture of Cassiopeia patches means you’ll probably spend a lot of time in this window, and it’s powerful and well laid out. It’s a shame, then, that there’s some real jank to the level fader controls – it can be really hard to get hold of them with the mouse pointer, particularly if you’ve previously pulled one all the way down.

Finally, there’s SOUND MENU, which allows you to swap different sound layers in or out. The options for each layer are neatly labelled and categorized, so if you’re the experimental type you’ll find hundreds of options allowing for many thousands of permutations.

## What About The Rest Of The Bundle?

Landlord Stabs uses the same basic design to deliver a selection of over 500 chord and stab-based presets. Named after the legendary Landlord stab , this instrument goes further, with organs, orchestral-style, and other hits. If you’re after rave leads, look no further, but there’s much more to it than that.

Zerotone 6 next, and this one is as close as the bundle gets to a conventional synthesizer, but still very much based on layered elements and inventive modulations. It gets its core sounds from two analogue synths – the Sequential Circuits Prophet-10 and Studio Electronics SE-1, judging from the images – allowing real-time blending, bending, and cross-modulation of the various waveforms in a custom granular engine. It sounds great, offers a bunch of usable presets, and has oodles of scope for user sound design.

Finally we come to The Riga Piano. At first glance this feels like a bit of a wild card, but when you listen you realize how this slots into the package. Most high-profile modern music is pretty in-your-face and highly produced and polished, and this instrument applies that same principle to a range of pianos.

It offers a surprisingly huge range of styles and tones that have one thing in common. They’re big, bold, and will cut through the mix with almost no extra effort.

## Production Suite 1 In Conclusion

All of which pretty much sums up this whole package. Whether you’re a jobbing producer on a deadline for a client or sitting down in the studio with a blank screen looking for inspiration, the way the bundle puts a universe of recognizable and ready-to-rock presets at your fingertips has real value.

Speaking of value, at $420, going up to $750 after the launch window, this is no budget purchase. Even Cassiopeia on its own sets you back $375 at the time of review, rising to $500 later. Does it all justify the price tag?

On an objective level, yes. There’s clearly been a huge amount of work put into this collection. Getting this much sampled audio material together and building an instrument of this scale is incredibly time-consuming and labour-intensive, as is the preset creation, optimization, calibration, and testing required to produce this level of quality and consistency. But, as with any studio purchase, what something’s ‘worth’ should really depend on its utility to the buyer.

If you’re a casual producer and are totally happy with your existing suite of instruments, then it’s not a game-changing purchase for you. You’ll probably have a lot of fun, but may not get your money’s worth. Likewise, those chasing organic and acoustic sounds are advised to steer clear. But if you’re a professional dance producer who wants a constant source of inspiration and cannot have too many release-ready patches to slot into your busy studio schedule … there’s a lot to like here.

The whole package drips with modern studio production experience and you can tell that the person behind it knows how to produce highly polished electronic tracks, fast. # Cassiopeia Production Suite 1 Bundle

Reviews » Gear/Software » Cassiopeia Production Suite 1 Bundle Cassiopeia Production Suite 1 Bundle Share Facebook Twitter WhatsApp These four Kontakt instruments from Soundsphat deliver thousands of highly editable, release-ready presets. Let’s see what sample-based sound design has to offer your productions.

Software synthesizers completely revolutionized the way music was made, and the sound of almost every genre of music has changed as a result. But arguably at least as influential to the music we hear today were sample-based instruments, such as those made for NI’s Kontakt.

From meticulously recreated playable orchestras to special effects and sound design tools, everybody with a computer can produce more complex, modulatable tones in seconds than the entire BBC Radiophonic Workshop could manage in decades.

But with so many analogue-modelled soft synths on the market today, it feels like we rarely use sampled instruments for our core sounds. Which is where the Cassiopeia bundle of Kontakt instruments comes in.

Guided by Grammy-nominated Christian Beat Hirt, Soundsphat aims to deliver a definitive selection of production-ready presets, complete with performance and modulation options, and all of the envelope, filter, and effects controls you could desire.

## Production Suite 1 Overview

There are four instruments in the package: Cassiopeia, Landlord Stabs, Zerotone 6, and The Riga Piano. Each has its own sonic concept but all share a similar interface and layer-based approach to sound design, so we’ll devote most of this review to the headline instrument, Cassiopeia, then explain how the others each riff on this concept.

Cassiopeia is based around four sound layers. The first two play host to the core sound layers like multisampled analogue synth layers, custom wavetables, acoustic-instrument-sourced waveforms, and more. The second two are sound-design-focused layers, including everything from bird calls and bells to subs and metal clangs. You can even add your own layers.

In terms of content, the headline figures are pretty impressive: a 422 GB library size (compressed to around 350 GB on your drive) with 58,000 samples, 120 custom wavetables, and 3,922 multisampled patches.

The sound design is top-notch throughout and the biggest selling point of this package by far. You could absolutely make complete, great-sounding tracks with nothing more than the sounds on offer here. Every kind of patch is covered, from basses and leads to pads and effects. And they’re incredibly polished, rich, slathered in effects, and ready to use.

For all that variety, though, this collection does very much have a distinct vibe. And it’s aimed squarely at the dancefloor and energetic playlists, so if you don’t like those kinds of sounds, this probably won’t be your bag.

## Cassiopeia In Use

Once you’ve found your sounds there is a powerful range of editing options.

The main interface is fairly uncomplicated with an X-Y modulation matrix for simultaneous real-time modulation of multiple effects and some headline parameters such as pitch bend range, filter cutoff and resonance, tone, volume, and velocity sensitivity. Plus buttons to add/mute each of the four sound layers that make up a Cassiopeia patch.

There are then six editing pages. EDIT offers up various controls. For example, polyphony, portamento, and a chord maker feature. Then you can apply up to nine effects: Reverb/convolution, Room, Comp, Delay, EQ, Tape, Chorus, Flanger, and Phaser, with detailed controls for each.

Next comes ADSR, offering up assignable envelope control for volume, cutoff, and pitch of each individual layer. This is very welcome, but unfortunately brings us to the first of only two gripes about this synth. The way you assign the envelopes to the layers is really unintuitive, and hard to understand even after reading the manual. You use the same on/off button to assign a voice to an envelope group as you do to call up that voice’s individual envelope settings. It’s definitely worth revisiting in an update.

Speaking of which, the LFO page has the same sound-shaping benefits and confusing assignment system as ADSR.

Luckily the ARP window is not confusing at all, offering a powerful and intuitive step-sequence-style programmer and all of the swing and timing controls you’d hope for. There’s even a randomize function.

It’s no surprise, then, that some of the most satisfying patches in the whole instrument are found in the ARP preset category – there’s just something fundamentally usable about them, enhanced by the top-tier sound design of each patch. Just keep an eye on the timing as you’ll find most arp-based patches need between −5 and −20 ms of track delay to slot into a project.

The MIX window comes next, with level and pan controls for each of the four layers, plus individual per-layer controls for things like pitch (semitones and cents), high- and low-pass filters, and Body and Silk (for boosting or easing low-mid and high-mid frequencies, respectively).

The layer-based architecture of Cassiopeia patches means you’ll probably spend a lot of time in this window, and it’s powerful and well laid out. It’s a shame, then, that there’s some real jank to the level fader controls – it can be really hard to get hold of them with the mouse pointer, particularly if you’ve previously pulled one all the way down.

Finally, there’s SOUND MENU, which allows you to swap different sound layers in or out. The options for each layer are neatly labelled and categorized, so if you’re the experimental type you’ll find hundreds of options allowing for many thousands of permutations.

## What About The Rest Of The Bundle?

Landlord Stabs uses the same basic design to deliver a selection of over 500 chord and stab-based presets. Named after the legendary Landlord stab , this instrument goes further, with organs, orchestral-style, and other hits. If you’re after rave leads, look no further, but there’s much more to it than that.

Zerotone 6 next, and this one is as close as the bundle gets to a conventional synthesizer, but still very much based on layered elements and inventive modulations. It gets its core sounds from two analogue synths – the Sequential Circuits Prophet-10 and Studio Electronics SE-1, judging from the images – allowing real-time blending, bending, and cross-modulation of the various waveforms in a custom granular engine. It sounds great, offers a bunch of usable presets, and has oodles of scope for user sound design.

Finally we come to The Riga Piano. At first glance this feels like a bit of a wild card, but when you listen you realize how this slots into the package. Most high-profile modern music is pretty in-your-face and highly produced and polished, and this instrument applies that same principle to a range of pianos.

It offers a surprisingly huge range of styles and tones that have one thing in common. They’re big, bold, and will cut through the mix with almost no extra effort.

## Production Suite 1 In Conclusion

All of which pretty much sums up this whole package. Whether you’re a jobbing producer on a deadline for a client or sitting down in the studio with a blank screen looking for inspiration, the way the bundle puts a universe of recognizable and ready-to-rock presets at your fingertips has real value.

Speaking of value, at $420, going up to $750 after the launch window, this is no budget purchase. Even Cassiopeia on its own sets you back $375 at the time of review, rising to $500 later. Does it all justify the price tag?

On an objective level, yes. There’s clearly been a huge amount of work put into this collection. Getting this much sampled audio material together and building an instrument of this scale is incredibly time-consuming and labour-intensive, as is the preset creation, optimization, calibration, and testing required to produce this level of quality and consistency. But, as with any studio purchase, what something’s ‘worth’ should really depend on its utility to the buyer.

If you’re a casual producer and are totally happy with your existing suite of instruments, then it’s not a game-changing purchase for you. You’ll probably have a lot of fun, but may not get your money’s worth. Likewise, those chasing organic and acoustic sounds are advised to steer clear. But if you’re a professional dance producer who wants a constant source of inspiration and cannot have too many release-ready patches to slot into your busy studio schedule … there’s a lot to like here.

The whole package drips with modern studio production experience and you can tell that the person behind it knows how to produce highly polished electronic tracks, fast. And as much as we’ve focused on the package as a preset factory, that layering approach delivers an unexpectedly huge amount of customization and creativity for a sample-based instrument.

In the end, if these kinds of electronic sounds are up your street, you will be hard-pressed to find a more comprehensive, playable, or better-sounding selection of customizable presets.

You can find a huge range of preset demos for each instrument in the bundle on Soundsphat’s website .

And here’s a little jam we put together using nothing but unedited presets from Cassiopeia, Landlord Stabs, and Zerotone 6.

## The Verdict

Price: $420 ($750 after launch)

Purchase: Soundsphat Cassiopeia Production Suite 1

### The Final Word

A vast library of release-ready dancefloor sounds with surprising depth for a sample-based instrument.

# Google Gemini bekommt ein Chat-Archiv

## Google Gemini bekommt ein Chat-Archiv

von Benjamin Mamerow 24. Nov. 2026 | 0

Die Seitenleiste von Gemini ist nach geraumer Zeit der Nutzung ziemlich vollgepappt mit Entwürfen, Fragen zur Steuererklärung und allem, was ihr sonst so in der Vergangenheit gefragt habt. Zum Aufräumen gibt es bislang nur die Option des Löschens, dann sind aber auch eventuell noch nützliche Antworten weg. Android Authority hat in der aktuellen Version der Google-App nun eine Funktion zum Archivieren von Chats gefunden .

Ein langer Druck auf einen Eintrag in der Seitenleiste öffnet demnach ein Menü, dort steht dann die Option zum Archivieren. Danach verschwindet der Chat aus der normalen Übersicht, bleibt aber gespeichert. Gemini bekommt einen Filter für archivierte Chats direkt in der Seitenleiste, damit ihr jene dann auch bei Gelegenheit schnell wieder hervorholen könnt.

Im Programmcode steckt noch ein zweiter Eintrag namens Spaces. Hierbei handelt es sich um einen dedizierten Button, ein Klick darauf wechselt in den Aufgaben-Tab und trägt im Textfeld die Aufforderung ein, einen neuen Bereich anzulegen. Mehr passiert aktuell aber nicht, denn auf den Servern von Google fehlt derzeit die dafür nötige Technik. Möglich, dass sich dahinter ein gemeinsamer Arbeitsbereich für Dokumente verbirgt, ähnlich wie bei ChatGPT.

articleBody:
# One terminal command gave my forgotten Android device a desk job

My kitchen junk drawer used to hold takeout menus and coupons, but it has since become a storage spot for old tablets or phones. Like me, you probably have a few devices lying around that are perfectly functional, but might not meet your daily driving needs. It’s tucked away out of view, meant to live out the rest of its life in a drawer before finally being cleaned out and donated the next time someone opens the drawer and asks why you’re holding on to outdated, unused devices. Thankfully, PhoneBox has a solution. You weren’t hoarding old tech; you were waiting for the proper use.

I had an old AllDoCube iPlay 50 mini Pro 8.4-inch tablet that seemed like the perfect candidate. I bought the tablet second-hand as a possible big-screen gaming and emulation tablet to use with a telescopic control deck, but I quickly found I vastly preferred just using a dedicated device. Since that realization, this decent little unit has lived its life like so many other forgotten devices in a drawer.

## Installation is a doddle

Getting PhoneBox up and running on my tablet and PC couldn’t have been any simpler. After making sure that the Android tablet was in developer mode, the process was as simple as plugging the tablet into my PC via USB and executing a single copied command in my Linux terminal. The script downloaded the PhoneBox 0.9.29 software for my PC, verified the downloaded checksum against the release, and walked me through a few quick Y/N installation questions. The script offers to create a systemd user service so the desktop agent launches after initial login, and even asks if you’d like it to install the PhoneBox APK to your connected Android device.

I already had developer mode initialized on the tablet, but had to go back and allow ADB over USB in settings. The total installation time from copying the script from the project website to everything running on my PC and tablet was less than a minute. The app is MIT-licensed , works on Android 5.0 or later, and requires sideloading since it is not available on the Google Play Store .

The installation script also prints its own uninstall script before it finishes. So often these days, getting rid of an unwanted app feels more difficult than installing it, so I appreciate the straightforward approach the developer has implemented.

## What your device becomes

The first time you fire PhoneBox up, you get live performance and diagnostic information from your PC, along with several pages of optional content that can be tweaked for your local setup to display information that’s pertinent to your uses.

Where PhoneBox really starts to shine is the widget catalog. A collection of free add-ons that can be added as pages to the tablet’s cycling page layouts. There are more general widgets like RSS feeds that display news highlights from your chosen sources, or simple displays like timers or world clocks.

I opted for a few different widgets that caught my eye. One let me view my library of installed Steam titles and launch them on my PC with a simple tap of the tablet screen. Another allows me to control smart home entities hosted by my Home Assistant server. I was controlling the lights in my office from my tablet within seconds of adding the widget. It’s brilliant.

Setting up additional widgets is as simple as adding them to the page layout from the PC’s web interface and hitting save. As soon as I updated things from the PC, the connected tablet immediately began reflecting the changes. I haven’t had the chance to test most of the 131 current options in the widget catalog, but the ones I did were simple to modify and worked on the first try.

## Some frictions

While I didn’t have any major issues with PhoneBox, I did notice a couple of early annoyances along the way. Windows users should be aware that the PC companion app on that OS is currently unsigned, and they should expect a SmartScreen notification when attempting to install the software.

All control settings live in the web interface rather than the phone or tablet you’re connecting. When I first started messing with PhoneBox, I noticed it displayed my weather location as Tallinn. Nothing against the capital of Estonia, but that’s not weather information that does me much good here in the US Midwest. When I went into the widget settings to change the report location, there was nothing to be found. It turns out that you have to change those settings from the general user preferences section rather than within the widget itself. Not a deal-breaker by any means, but a slight hiccup for someone who was new to the software.

Connecting the Android tablet with my PC over USB was totally painless, but I never got the wireless route to work in my testing. Users are meant to generate a QR code from the PhoneBox web interface on their PC, and connect it to their device by scanning the code with their phone/tablet. Every time I tried to scan the code from my device’s camera app, the tablet refused. There’s no QR scanner built into the PhoneBox app, so if your camera app won’t cooperate, the documented path dead-ends. USB was my intended route anyway and works great, but if you’re planning a wireless-only setup, be prepared for possible friction. The documented flow depends on your device camera opening the pairing link, and mine wasn’t in the mood.

These minor gripes should be smoothed over before the release of 1.0. The project is early, but it seems to be moving quickly. I tested and installed PhoneBox version 0.9.29, which was one of several releases pushed to the project’s GitHub in as many days. One item of history worth knowing: On November 20, the project published a high-severity security advisory covering versions 0.9.23 and earlier. The vulnerability potentially allowed another app running on the connected Android device to execute commands or receive stored credentials from the host PC. The flaw no longer existed by the time I tested the package in version 0.9.29, but it’s a good reminder that you’re installing something with deep system access and should exercise appropriate caution.

## Is it worth trying?

As long as you’re part of the group that has an old phone or tablet lying around somewhere, and these days I expect that most of us are, then it’s an emphatic yes. Repurposing old devices to find new lives is one of the things that keeps me a tech hobbyist. I love finding genuinely useful and practical applications for devices that may have been pushed aside by their manufacturers in favor of the latest and greatest in the lineup.

PhoneBox took a tablet that was destined to live in a junk drawer before being gathered up for a spring donation run, and gave it a new lease on life. I haven’t spent a single penny, and now I have a useful secondary display on my desk. The tablet is powered via a dedicated USB port on my PC, and only goes to sleep when my main monitor displays do. Go dig through those mystery drawers, because this one is worthwhile.

articleBody:
Kaleidoscopic [patterns](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/patterns/) adorn the exterior of this [pavilion](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/pavilions-tag/) in Doha, Qatar, designed by artist Gerhard Richter with US studio [Selldorf Architects](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/selldorf-architects/) as an [art gallery.](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/galleries/)

Simply called Doha Pavilion, the psychedelic structure was conceived a work of both art and architecture for MIA Park – a public space outside the [Museum of Islamic Art by IM Pei](https://www.dezeen.com/2025/01/14/museum-of-islamic-art-im-pei-21st-century-architecture/).

### Photographs

Previous

Next

### Photographs

Close

It serves as a permanent pavilion for the site and as a gallery for Richter's own work.

Richter designed the Doha Pavilion with[Selldorf Architects](https://www.selldorf.com/) as a reference to his Strip paintings – a series that involved digitally dividing his Abstract Painting artwork into vertical stripes, building on his earlier explorations of colour, pattern and repetition.

"My trip to Doha in 2013 came two years into developing my Strip paintings, and the city’s architecture and history sparked an idea for a pavilion that could unite the thematic threads of that body of work," said Richter.

"The pavilion’s exterior features decorative tiles based on the patterns that first led me to the Strips," he continued. "Doha is the right place and the only place for my pavilion.”

Doha Pavilion has a six-sided form, wrapped in psychedelic tiles displaying repeating, kaleidoscopic patterns that recall geometries seen in Islamic art, nodding to the project's context.

Selldorf Architects founder Annabelle Selldorf said the design reflects a "profound culmination of many years of [Richter's] research into abstraction".

"I am grateful for the welcome that Gerhard Richter extended to me, and for the wonderful dialogue that ensued, as my studio made manifest the work that had existed in his mind," she said.

"This pavilion is the profound culmination of many years of his research into abstraction, with intensely physical patterns that invite you to immerse yourself in their endlessness," she continued.

"The more I look at them, the more fascinating they become to me as an architectural space to experience."

Inside, Richter's paintings and sculptures are displayed throughout the hexagonal gallery space. This includes both archival and new works made especially for the pavilion.

Among the new works is the Strip Tower – a freestanding tripartite sculpture.

[Read: David Chipperfield Architects builds concrete gallery around singular artwork in Germany](https://www.dezeen.com/2026/10/20/anselm-kiefer-pavilion-david-chipperfield-architects-germany/)

The opening of Doha Pavilion coincides with the inaugural edition of Rubaiya Qatar 2026, which is an international visual arts quadrennial.

Elsewhere, [Selldorf Architects recently completed the controversial remodel of the National Gallery’s Sainsbury Wing](https://www.dezeen.com/2025/05/06/sainsbury-wing-renovation-national-gallery-selldorf-architects-london/). In an interview with Dezeen after the opening, founder Selldorf said that ["what matters is I know why we did things"](https://www.dezeen.com/2025/05/06/annabelle-selldorf-gallery-renovation-sainsbury-wing-frick-collection-interview/).

title: Neutralität im Klassenzimmer

articleBody:
Anfang November hat das Landesschulamt Sachsen-Anhalt die [Abmahnung des Lehrers Max Heckel aus dessen Personalakte gelöscht](https://www.spiegel.de/panorama/bildung/afd-in-sachsen-anhalt-ein-lehrer-eine-abmahnung-und-der-streit-ueber-die-neutralitaetspflicht-a-2a9dc291-a9d7-46fd-b6ce-00fcc109998c), die es ihm wegen AfD-kritischer Aussagen im Unterricht vor knapp eineinhalb Jahren erteilt hatte. Drei Wochen vor dem geplanten Gerichtstermin am Arbeitsgericht Magdeburg hat sich damit der Gegenstand der gerichtlichen Auseinandersetzung erledigt. Der Fall gibt dennoch Anlass, sich vor Augen zu führen, was der Begriff der Neutralität in der Schule aus rechtlicher Sicht bedeutet, wozu Lehrkräfte im Unterricht verpflichtet sind und wie sie sich verhalten müssen, wenn parteipolitische Positionen thematisiert werden.

Der Neutralitätsbegriff in der Schule hat einen unmissverständlichen verfassungsrechtlichen Rahmen. Er fordert von den Lehrkräften, sich aktiv und ständig zur freiheitlich demokratischen Grundordnung sowie den verfassungsrechtlichen Grundwerten zu bekennen. Eine normative Wertneutralität umfasst der Begriff gerade nicht. Zudem ist es Lehrkräften verboten, in religiös-weltanschaulicher sowie parteipolitischer Hinsicht Druck auf die Schüler*innen auszuüben und ihnen eigene Positionen aufzudrängen. Hieraus abzuleiten, dass menschenverachtende Positionen in der Schule als legitim dargestellt werden müssen, ist falsch und verfassungswidrig.

## Der Fall Max Heckel

Mit dem Klagegegenstand hat sich jetzt auch die Hoffnung auf eine verbindliche Klarstellung der rechtlichen Fragen erledigt, die angesichts der [verbreiteten](https://www.spiegel.de/panorama/bildung/lehrkraefte-umfrage-die-grosse-angst-vor-politischen-debatten-im-klassenzimmer-a-3454943f-9ceb-42c5-b046-2e1c419fa608) und [von der AfD bewusst herbeigeführten](https://verfassungsblog.de/lehrermeldeportale-darf-der-staat-nicht-akzeptieren/) Verunsicherung von Lehrkräften über den Fall hinaus bedeutsam gewesen wäre. [Seit 2018](https://www.gew.de/die-meldeportale-der-afd) betreibt die AfD online Meldeportale unter dem Titel „Neutrale Schule“, die dazu auffordern, angeblich neutralitätswidriges Verhalten von Lehrkräften bei den AfD-Fraktionen zu melden. Das Ziel dieses Vorgehens scheint die Einschüchterung von Lehrkräften zu sein, die Positionen der AfD im Unterricht kritisieren.

Der Lehrer Max Heckel wurde im Unterricht an einer Sekundarschule in Stendal von einem Schüler gefragt, ob er bei der letzten Bundestagswahl die AfD gewählt habe. In einem [Spiegel-Interview](https://www.spiegel.de/panorama/bildung/afd-der-lehrer-max-heckel-aus-stendal-will-einen-praezedenzfall-schaffen-a-20444482-fb06-4259-bea5-d7ad40ac0955) berichtet Heckel den Verlauf des hieraus entstandenen Gesprächs über die politischen Positionen der AfD: Selbst nicht die AfD gewählt zu haben, begründete er mit der Steuerpolitik der AfD sowie ihren Plänen zum Abbau schulischer Inklusion und zur Durchsetzung von „Remigration“. Dabei stellte er Vergleiche zu den Positionen anderer politischer Parteien an und erklärte, worauf sich seine persönliche Position gründet. Hierzu zeigte er den Schüler*innen eine Statistik des Leibniz-Instituts für Europäische Wirtschaftsforschung, gab ein Zitat von Björn Höcke wieder, bildete Beispiele zur praktischen Umsetzung von Inklusion in der Schule und erklärte, woher der „Remigrationsbegriff“ stammt und was er bedeutet. Zudem betonte er der Klasse gegenüber, dass für ihn alle Schüler*innen gleich viel wert sind und er inklusives Lernen für sinnvoll hält – und nahm damit implizit Bezug auf Werte wie die Menschenwürde aus Art. 1 Abs. 1 GG und das in der UN-Behindertenrechtskonvention verankerte Recht auf inklusive Bildung. Zum Ende des Gesprächs sagte er, wenn man die AfD wähle, müsse man „a) reich, b) frei von Moral oder c) nicht bei Verstand sein“, fügte aber auch hinzu, dass es natürlich trotzdem jedem freistehe, die AfD zu wählen, der zu einem anderen Schluss käme.

Fünf Wochen später erteilte das Schulamt Sachsen-Anhalt ihm eine Abmahnung und vertrat darin die Ansicht, dass Heckel mit seinen Äußerungen die Neutralitätspflicht verletzt habe und sie nicht der Aufklärung, sondern allein dem Ziel gedient hätten, die Schüler*innen davon zu überzeugen, nicht die AfD zu wählen. Zuvor hatte der AfD-Spitzenkandidat Ulrich Siegmund, dessen Ehefrau an derselben Schule arbeitet, im [Landtag von einem „Fall in Stendal“ berichtet](https://www.spiegel.de/panorama/bildung/afd-in-sachsen-anhalt-ein-lehrer-eine-abmahnung-und-der-streit-ueber-die-neutralitaetspflicht-a-2a9dc291-a9d7-46fd-b6ce-00fcc109998c) und mitgeteilt, die AfD habe eine Dienstaufsichtsbeschwerde erhoben und nach einiger Zeit noch einmal Druck auf das Landesschulamt ausgeübt. In der anschließenden Auseinandersetzung drohte das Schulamt dem Lehrer mit Kündigung. Schließlich entschied sich Max Heckel, rechtlich gegen die Abmahnung vorzugehen, um die strittigen Fragen verbindlich klären zu lassen: War die Abmahnung rechtmäßig? Durfte er das geschilderte Gespräch auf diese Weise mit den Schüler*innen führen? Durfte er sagen, AfD-Wähler*innen müssten wohl „reich, frei von Moral oder nicht bei Verstand“ sein, oder hat er damit die Grundsätze der schulischen Neutralität verletzt? Welche Anforderungen bestehen konkret an das Verhalten von Lehrkräften im Unterrichtsgespräch über parteipolitische Positionen?

## Der rechtliche Rahmen der Neutralität in der Schule

Es gibt in Deutschland keine explizit normierte Definition des Begriffs „Neutralität in der Schule“. Stattdessen ergibt sich der Inhalt des Neutralitätsgebots aus dem Grundgesetz, den Landesverfassungen, den Schulgesetzen der Bundesländer, dem Beamten- und Arbeitsrecht sowie den internationalen Menschenrechtsverträgen.

In Art. 7 Abs. 1 GG enthält die Verfassung den Bildungs- und Erziehungsauftrag des Staates. Er verpflichtet den Staat dazu, ein funktionsfähiges Schulsystem sicherzustellen, das Wissen, Fertigkeiten und soziale Kompetenzen vermittelt. Dieser Auftrag dient dem Ziel, eine chancengleiche Entwicklung der Kinder und Jugendlichen zu eigenverantwortlichen Persönlichkeiten zu ermöglichen, die sich an demokratischen Prozessen beteiligen. Die Schulgesetze der Bundesländer stellen klar, dass die Schule einen Auftrag zur demokratischen Bildung und Erziehung der Schüler*innen auf der normativen Grundlage der Verfassung hat. So bestimmt beispielsweise § 1 des Schulgesetzes Sachsen-Anhalt:

> „(1) Der Auftrag der Schule wird bestimmt durch das Grundgesetz der Bundesrepublik Deutschland und die Verfassung des Landes Sachsen-Anhalt. […]
> (2) In Erfüllung dieses Auftrages ist die Schule insbesondere gehalten,
> die Schülerinnen und Schüler zur Achtung der Würde des Menschen, zur Selbstbestimmung in Verantwortung gegenüber Andersdenkenden, zur Anerkennung und Bindung an ethische Werte, zur Achtung religiöser Überzeugungen, zu verantwortlichem Gebrauch der Freiheit und zu friedlicher Gesinnung zu erziehen,
> die Schülerinnen und Schüler auf die Übernahme politischer und sozialer Verantwortung im Sinne der freiheitlich-demokratischen Grundordnung vorzubereiten,
> […]
> den Schülerinnen und Schülern Kenntnisse, Fähigkeiten und Werthaltungen zu vermitteln, wonach niemand aus Gründen des Geschlechts, der sexuellen Identität, einer Behinderung, der Abstammung oder wegen seiner Sprache, seiner Heimat und Herkunft, seines Glaubens oder seiner religiösen oder politischen Anschauungen oder aus rassistischen oder antisemitischen Gründen benachteiligt oder bevorzugt werden darf; über die Möglichkeiten des Abbaus von Diskriminierungen und Benachteiligungen ist aufzuklären,
> […]
> die Schülerinnen und Schüler zu Toleranz gegenüber kultureller Vielfalt und zur Völkerverständigung zu erziehen sowie zu befähigen, die Bedeutung der Heimat in einem geeinten Deutschland, einem gemeinsamen Europa und einer globalisierten Welt zu erkennen.“ (Herv. d. Verf.)

## Aktives Bekenntnis zur freiheitlich demokratischen Grundordnung

Lehrkräfte üben den schulgesetzlich konkretisierten Bildungs- und Erziehungsauftrag des Staates für diesen aus. Dabei sind sie als verbeamtete Lehrkräfte (§ 33 Abs. 1 S. 2 BeamtStG) sowie als angestellte Lehrkräfte (§ 3 TV-L) gleichermaßen dazu verpflichtet, „sich durch ihr gesamtes Verhalten zur freiheitlich demokratischen Grundordnung zu bekennen“. Die freiheitlich demokratische Grundordnung, auch als „Ordnung der Menschenwürde“ bezeichnet, beinhaltet die Menschenwürde aus Art. 1 Abs. 1 GG, das Demokratieprinzip aus Art. 20 Abs. 1 und 2 GG sowie das Rechtsstaatsprinzip aus Art. 20 Abs. 3 GG. Sie ist sowohl im Grundgesetz als auch in den Landesverfassungen fest verankert. Ihr Verhalten im Unterricht hieran auszurichten, ist die fundamentale Pflicht der Lehrkräfte. Daraus folgt, dass sie sich aktiv gegen jede Form gruppenbezogener Menschenfeindlichkeit wie rassifizierende, antisemitische oder antimuslimische Äußerungen stellen müssen. Und: Verfassungswidrige Positionen müssen Lehrkräfte deutlich als solche benennen und als verfassungswidrig zurückweisen. Das gilt gleichermaßen, wenn es sich dabei um Positionen handelt, die von politischen Parteien und ihren Mandatsträger*innen vertreten werden. Wer demgegenüber behauptet, menschenverachtende Positionen müssten in der Schule aufgrund des Neutralitätsgebots unkommentiert bleiben oder sogar als legitime Äußerungen akzeptiert werden, hat hierfür keinerlei rechtliche Grundlage – im Gegenteil: Das Grundgesetz, die Landesverfassungen, die Schulgesetze sowie das Beamten- und Arbeitsrecht machen für Lehrkräfte und Schulleitungen sehr deutlich, dass ein aktives Bekenntnis zu den grundgesetzlichen Werten und deren Vermittlung im Unterricht ihre unmissverständliche Pflicht ist. Entsprechend bestätigte das [OVG Berlin-Brandenburg im Januar 2026](https://gerichtsentscheidungen.brandenburg.de/gerichtsentscheidung/28169), dass eine Schulleitung in Brandenburg einer Schülerin untersagen durfte, ihr Betriebspraktikum im Büro eines Bundestagsabgeordneten der AfD zu absolvieren, der dem als gesichert rechtsextrem eingestuften Landesverband der AfD Brandenburg angehört. Das Gericht stellte klar: Die Schulleitung durfte zu dem Schluss kommen, dass das geplante Praktikum bei einer Vereinigung, die aktiv die Beseitigung von Verfassungsgrundsätzen der freiheitlich-demokratischen Grundordnung anstrebt, mit dem Bildungs- und Erziehungsauftrag nicht vereinbar ist.

## Politische Inhalte in der Schule

Werden politische Inhalte und Parteien im Unterricht thematisiert, kommt die parteipolitische Neutralität der Lehrkräfte zum Tragen. Neben der individuellen Meinungsfreiheit der Schüler*innen und Lehrkräfte gilt auch das Grundrecht der politischen Parteien auf Chancengleichheit aus Art. 21 Abs. 1 GG. Staatliche Stellen, wozu auch die öffentlichen Schulen zählen, dürfen politische Parteien (die nicht verboten sind) nicht benachteiligen. Hieraus folgt, dass Lehrkräfte politische Parteien nicht pauschal befürworten oder abwerten dürfen. Sie müssen den Unterricht sachlich und ausgewogen gestalten, unterschiedliche Ansichten und Meinungen zur Geltung kommen lassen und tolerant gegenüber abweichenden Ansichten sein – und sie dürfen die Schüler*innen nicht missionieren oder indoktrinieren. Diese Anforderungen an die Unterrichtsgestaltung gelten gleichermaßen für parteipolitische und religiös-weltanschauliche Fragen. Gleichzeitig müssen sie ihre eigenen Meinungen und Positionen nicht leugnen, diese aber als eigene Standpunkte ausweisen und zur Disposition stellen. Als Richtschnur für die Gestaltung politischer Bildung in der Schule wird häufig der Beutelsbacher Konsens von 1976 herangezogen, der das Ziel formuliert, die Schüler*innen geschützt vor Indoktrination in die Lage zu versetzen, anhand gemeinsamer Auseinandersetzung mit kontroversen Themen aus Politik und Wissenschaft unterschiedliche politische Fragen und ihre eigene Interessenlage zu analysieren.

## Bedeutung für die schulische Praxis

Lehrkräfte dürfen ihre persönliche Meinung zu Positionen politischer Parteien mitteilen und erklären, wie sie sich ihre Meinung gebildet haben – insbesondere, wenn sie von Schüler*innen danach gefragt werden. Fragen im Unterricht dürfen sie auch zum Anlass nehmen, die Wahlprogramme und Ziele von Parteien, deren gesellschaftlichen und historischen Kontext sowie Äußerungen von Parteimitgliedern zu thematisieren. Entscheidend sind die sachliche und ausgewogene Unterrichtsgestaltung sowie die Klarstellung, dass es sich um eine persönliche Meinung handelt, die weder absolut noch allgemeingültig ist.

Vielleicht hätte das Arbeitsgericht Magdeburg geurteilt, dass Max Heckel mit der Formulierung, wer die AfD wähle, sei „reich, frei von Moral oder nicht bei Verstand“ die Grenzen der Sachlichkeit und Ausgewogenheit im Sinne der schulischen Neutralität überschritten hat, und die Abmahnung insofern rechtmäßig war. Dann wäre klar, dass Lehrkräfte auf eine derartige Formulierung verzichten sollten. Vielleicht aber auch nicht. Vielleicht hätte das Gericht auch entschieden, dass die Anforderungen an die sachliche und ausgewogene Unterrichtsgestaltung angesichts des Gesamtkontexts der Äußerung sowie des Gesprächsverhaltens des Lehrers gewahrt worden sind.

Jedenfalls hätte das Gericht Folgendes erkennen und feststellen müssen: Allein die rechtliche Einordnung der Formulierung, wer die AfD wähle, sei „reich, frei von Moral oder nicht bei Verstand“ ist strittig. Mit seinem restlichen Verhalten hat Max Heckel bei der Besprechung parteipolitischer Inhalte nicht gegen die Grundsätze der schulischen Neutralität verstoßen. Es rechtfertigt daher keinerlei Beanstandung oder Abmahnung. Für die Unterstellung des Schulamtes, die Äußerungen hätten nicht der Aufklärung, sondern allein der Überzeugung gedient, nicht die AfD zu wählen, bietet sein Verhalten keine Anhaltspunkte. Denn Max Heckel hat im Kern genau das getan, wozu er als Lehrkraft durch das Grundgesetz sowie die Landesverfassung und das Schulgesetz Sachsen-Anhalt verpflichtet ist: sich angesichts von verfassungswidrigen und menschenrechtsfeindlichen Positionierungen politischer Parteien – wie den Plänen der AfD zum Abbau schulischer Inklusion und der Durchsetzung von „Remigrationsplänen“ – aktiv zur Menschenwürde sowie zum Demokratie- und Rechtsstaatsprinzip zu bekennen und deren Grundsätze zu vermitteln. Das muss jede Lehrkraft tun.
