# Don’t Know What to Gift Your Friend? Start Here

In writing this guide on gift ideas for friends, I learned that there really is no catchall gift that will please everyone. Choosing these gifts, I thought back to some of the best self-care products and tech I’ve tested recently. I included the gadgets I reach for regularly, as well as those I’ve bought for family and friends after testing and loving them. So please use this guide as a starting point, keeping your friend’s personality, needs, and hobbies in mind as you shop for the right gifts.

After testing hundreds of products during my years on the WIRED Reviews team, these are the items I’d recommend to the friends on my own list. I’ve included self-care gifts like massagers, cozy gifts like an ultrasoft throw blanket, kitchen staples like a chef’s knife, and everything in between. There are many gifts at different price points, and they’re also categorized by gift type below. Be sure to check back often, as I will be updating this guide with versatile new picks as we get closer to gifting season.

Looking for more gift ideas? Don’t miss our other awesome gift guides as the holiday season ramps up.

- Best Tech Gifts
- Best Self-Care Gifts
- Best Cozy Gifts
- Best Kitchen Gifts
Updated November 24: I’ve updated links and prices and added more gifts from Sonos, HexClad, Owala, Grace & Stella, Ursa Major, Ole Henrickson, Lndn Gray, Lenox, Gumball Poodle, Galison, Brass Monkey, Tocca, WineWhiz, Nimble, and Belkin.

## Best Tech Gifts

### Go 5

Amazon

JBL

It’s my belief that everyone could use a small, portable Bluetooth speaker . Whether you want to sing along to your tunes in the shower or get the party going around a campfire, having a compact, Bluetooth-enabled speaker at the ready makes you everyone’s favorite party guest. At less than $60, I promise this li’l guy will be a hit as a gift (without breaking the bank). Plus, you can fully customize the design with images, text, and stickers if you want to make it more personalized for the giftee.

Google

### Home Speaker

Best Buy

Google Store

If you have a friend who could benefit from a smart speaker —to set timers, check the weather, or play tunes anywhere in the house without using their phone—this one is ideal, especially if they’re in the Google Home smart-home ecosystem. Plus, it comes in a range of fun colors.

### Echo Dot (5th Gen)

Amazon

This is our favorite budget-friendly Amazon Alexa smart-home speaker for homes in the Amazon/Alexa ecosystem. I’ve gotten one of these for my parents and sister-in-law, and it’s become their most-used gift.

### Champ Portable Charger

Shop

Amazon

After getting annoyed too many times when my best friend Sarah was late with a dead phone, I gave her this small portable charger . It’s fairly cheap, fits in her purse or tote , and keeps her phone charged, so I don’t have to worry about her being dead while I sip a martini waiting at the bar.

### 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand

Amazon

Shop

Best Buy

If your friend has a perpetually dying Apple Watch or iPhone, or even has limited outlets, a 3-in-1 charger is a thoughtful gift that saves space and keeps your friend’s tech juiced.

Courtesy of Sonos Save to wishlist Sonos

### Era 100 SL

Amazon

Sonos

If your friend wants a great home speaker for sound (not voice assistant tasks), the Sonos Era 100 SL is an excellent, microphone-free option. It is a huge step up in terms of sound quality—it can easily fill any smaller room (think apartment living) with rich, detailed instrumentation. And if they decide they love it, they can easily pair it with other Sonos speakers. — Harry Rabinowitz

## Best Self-Care Gifts

Chirp

### Sole Vibe

Shop

Chirp

This nifty gadget from wellness tech company Chirp is a godsend for anyone who’s always on their feet. It has two sides: One features a textured surface that targets pressure points, and the other has a heated, centralized oval that acts like a hot stone for targeted arch relief. The end has a USB-C charging port and buttons to adjust heat, vibration, and preset recovery programs, which use different heat and massage patterns for relief. I use this gadget almost daily, especially if I’ve been on my feet a lot that day. This is the perfect gift for someone who’s always asking for a foot massage.

### Halo

Shop

Chirp

This device uses TENS and EMS technology to deliver low-voltage electrical currents to motor nerves, which I feel improves my circulation and relaxes my muscles. I suffer from chronic back pain and joint overuse, and I’ve noticed improved mobility and circulation when using it consistently, especially in colder weather. This is the perfect gift for those who suffer from chronic pain or want targeted, post-workout relief.

- Courtesy of Therabody
Therabody

### TheraFace Depuffing Wand

Therabody

Shop

Amazon

If your friend is obsessed with using a gua sha tool, this is the ultimate upgrade. It uses the same techniques to encourage lymphatic drainage and features both cold settings to depuff and brighten and heat to increase circulation. I love to use it daily, and I gifted one to my skin-care-fanatic friend, who now uses it religiously.

### Fully Loaded Starter Set

Dollar Shave Club (Women's)

Dollar Shave Club (Men's)

I keep giving this luxe razor to my friends who want a better, razor-bump-free way to shave. The set comes with a ton of extras, including an exfoliating sugar scrub and a moisturizing shave oil. There are also men’s sets and subscription plans available.

### Wonders Collection Hand Cream Set

Shop

Amazon

I love a little self-care gift set, and this luxe box set of hand creams would also make an excellent white elephant gift . (And each is the perfect size for storing in a purse, car, and at work!)

### Ole’s Icons Skincare Bestseller Gift Set

Shop

Sephora

I’ve loved Ole Henriksen skin care products for years now, but this set of bestsellers focuses on moisturizing, making it especially perfect for gifting during cold, chapped-lips season.

Ursa Major

### Brighter Days Set

Shop

Ursa Major

I really love this brightening set, which packs a vitamin C serum and rich moisturizing face cream. It’s cute and makes a great gift. I also tested (and loved) the Recover & Glow Set if you’re looking to splurge.

grace & stella

### Dream Team Gift Set

Shop

Amazon

This surprisingly affordable skin care box set is the perfect gift for a friend who loves facial products or could use a little self-care. It includes a hydrating serum, energizing gold eye masks, a face mask, rose spray, face balm, and lip mask. Its focus on hydration is especially ideal for the dry winter months.

## Best Cozy Gifts

### Sleep Clock

Hatch

WIRED reviewer Boutayna Chokrane was sold on Hatch’s newest sunrise alarm clock, which also doubles as a sleep tracker . If your giftee doesn’t want to sleep with a wearable to get their sleep stats, this device uses motion-based tracking to provide passive sleep monitoring from their nightstand. It functions as a sunrise clock, a dimmable bedside light, and a sound machine , and it now captures data like sleep duration and stages, presented in interactive visuals. Boutayna loved the refreshing minimalist design, with no cameras or microphones watching you sleep. Best of all, your data is not locked behind a Hatch+ membership. If you have a friend who struggles with sleep or waking up, consider joining in the sunrise alarm clock trend and getting them this aesthetic bedside machine.

Bearaby

### Cotton Napper Weighted Blanket

Shop (15 pounds)

Bearaby (15 pounds)

I never want to get up when snuggling up with this weighted blanket, especially now that the weather has turned chilly around me. It’s woven from 100 percent cotton and comes in four different weights, from 10 to 25 pounds. Give your friend the gift of a cozy hug this winter with this seriously relaxing splurge.

Cocoon

### Classic Blanket

Shop

Cocoon

It’s my belief that you can never have too many cozy blankets for your couch. I’m always delighted when I’m gifted a new cozy blanket. Wearing this feels like being surrounded by a fluffy cloud. It’s made from a super-soft, shed-free polyester blend with added spandex for stretch, which also gives it a beautiful ribbing effect. I promise this gift will be fought over at the next movie night.

Gumball Poodle

### Grip Socks

Shop (Feral)

Shop (Spicy)

Gumball Poodle (All)

I hated getting socks for Christmas as a kid, but now I love them. These thick, tall winter socks feature fun, colorful designs and grippy bottoms to prevent slips. Plus, they’d also be an excellent, affordable white elephant gift .

### The Lenox Swan Collection Swan Figurine

Shop

Lenox

I love this porcelain diva. This swan has a super classic, old-school vibe, ideal for the tchotchke lover in your life. It’s great for storing trinkets, hair ties, or jewelry.

Lndn Gray

### Candle

Shop (Outlaw)

Shop (Badlands Motel)

These candles are ideal for a friend like me who hates artificial, super-sweet sugar-cookie candle scents. These soy wax candles have earthy notes of dry cedar and black amber, and they burn cleanly and evenly.

Galison

### Meowy Christmas 12 Days of Puzzles

Shop

Amazon

Call me a kid at heart, but I still get excited about Advent calendars . If you are exchanging gifts with friends before the holidays, this gift keeps on giving, with 12 mini cat-themed puzzles for the giftee to solve in the days leading up to the holiday. (They also have non-cat-themed Advent calendar puzzles if that’s more of your friend’s thing.)

## Best Kitchen Gifts

Material

### The 8-Inch Knife

Shop

Material

Everyone—I mean every single person—needs at least one great chef’s knife . This is probably the most important multipurpose kitchen tool—it can slice, dice, and chop ingredients with speed and precision. Your friend most likely could use a better knife for everyday cooking. Great chefs’ knives range from less than $100 to several hundred dollars, but I really like this mid-range, 8-inch knife from Material. It’s made from luxe Japanese high-carbon stainless steel for extra durability, with a matte, stain-resistant composite handle. Plus, if you buy from Material’s site, you can add an engraved message for a fun, more personal touch.

Caraway

### 4pc Fry & Sauté Set

Shop

Caraway

This is a splurge, but well worth it if your friend has been using old pans that tend to stick or flake. This four-piece nonstick ceramic set covers most of my everyday stovetop cooking: an 8-inch mini fry pan, 10.5-inch fry pan, 4.5-quart sauté pan, and a heavy-duty lid. I love these pans and haven’t needed another pan size since I’ve had them.

- Courtesy of Hydro Flask
Hydro Flask

### Coffee with Flex Sip Lid

Amazon

Hydro Flask (16-ounce)

This is pretty much everyone’s favorite travel mug on the Reviews team. In my opinion, you can never have too many options for taking drinks on the go. This one is low-maintenance, practically indestructible, and forgiving if you’re clumsy. Plus, the 16-ounce size fits most car cup holders, and the wide-mouth lids are interchangeable, so you can swap in a straw lid for cold beverages. If you buy directly from Hydro Flask, you can personalize it.

### Hybrid Fry Pan

shop

Hexclad

This is probably the best frying pan I’ve ever had. It’s nonstick and heats up evenly. At about $100, it’d be a great upgrade to get for your friend, especially if they’re using old pans or are a home chef.

Owala

### FreeSip Sway

Shop

Amazon

Everyone has this reusable bottle for good reason: It comes in fun colors, features triple-layer insulation, and lets you sip through a straw or tilt to drink. It’s a crowd-pleaser your friend could use in the car, at work, or in a gym bag.

Brass Monkey

### Oh What Googly-Eyed Fun Magnet Countdown Calendar

Shop

Brass Monkey

This would also make a great white elephant gift if you’re giving low-cost presents before the holidays. Help your friend get into the holiday spirit with this 12-day Advent calendar, which reveals cute little food-themed fridge magnets.

Lenox

### Poppies on Blue Kitten Cookie Jar

Shop

Lenox

When I die, put my ashes in this porcelain kitty. Until then, your friend can put cookies, bags of flour, sugar, coffee, beans, and more in this decorative holder. If your friend is a cat lover , or like me, loves a whimsical, not-totally-necessary decorative holder, this is a sure-fire win.

WineWhiz

### EVA Case Set

Amazon

If your friend is a wine enthusiast, or you want to impress at the next dinner party, I love these easy-to-use, accessible wine opener sets. This set includes an electric opener and aerator, plus a carrying case. WineWhiz also has its flagship ready-to-wrap box set , which I tested and liked, that makes a great gift and includes a foil cutter and vacuum sealer. But I love the idea of bringing a great bottle of wine and a fancy new opener with a cute carrying case to your holiday party and gifting both.

title: Lagebild - Zahl der Fälle von Gewalt gegen Frauen gestiegen
subtitle: In Deutschland ist im vergangenen Jahr fast jeden Tag eine Frau oder ein Mädchen getötet worden.
feedText: Wie aus zwei Lagebildern des Bundeskriminalamts zur Gewalt gegen Frauen hervorgeht, starben 342 Frauen und Mädchen durch Tötungsdelikte. Das sind rund elf Prozent mehr als im Vorjahr. Die Gefahr droht Mädchen und Frauen vor allem im Privaten.
articleBody:
# Lagebild - Zahl der Fälle von Gewalt gegen Frauen gestiegen

## "Gewalt gegen Frauen alltäglich"

## Gewalt vor allem im privaten Umfeld

## Haller: Rechtspraxis muss sich ändern

## Anstieg auch bei digitaler Gewalt

Bundesfrauenministerin Prien stellt das Lagebild Häusliche Gewalt vor. (IMAGO / BREUEL-BILD / IMAGO) Rund 60 Prozent waren Opfer von Gewalt in einer aktuellen oder früheren Partnerschaft sowie innerhalb der Familie. Insgesamt erfasste die Polizei im vergangenen Jahr fast 54.700 weibliche Opfer einer Sexualstraftat, knapp die Hälfte war minderjährig. Die Zahl der polizeilich registrierten Opfer häuslicher Gewalt stieg mit rund 280.000 auf einen neuen Höchststand. Einen deutlichen Anstieg gab es außerdem bei der Zahl weiblicher Opfer von digitaler Gewalt, und zwar um 15,7 Prozent. "Gewalt gegen Frauen alltäglich" Bundesjustizministerin Hubig und Bundesfrauenministerin Prien betonten, die Lagebilder zeigten, wie alltäglich Gewalt gegen Frauen sei. Das müsse sich ändern. Jede Frau habe ein Recht auf ein Leben ohne Angst und Gewalt. Bundesinnenminister Dobrindt erklärte, die Betroffenen müssten besser geschützt und Täter konsequent zur Verantwortung gezogen werden. Dobrindt kündigte an, konkrete Hilfsangebote stärken zu wollen sowie eine sichere Dokumentation von Übergriffen zu ermöglichen. Ziel sei, bislang verborgene Gewalt sichtbar zu machen. Gewalt vor allem im privaten Umfeld Die Beauftragte für Gewaltschutz beim Deutschen Frauenrat, Haller, betonte, die Gefahr für Mädchen und Frauen in Deutschland Opfer von Gewalt zu werden, sei sehr, sehr groß und vor allem im privaten Umfeld zu verorten. Die Sozialarbeiterin sagte im Deutschlandfunk , die stetig steigenden Zahlen seien zum einen darauf zurückzuführen, dass Männer mehr Macht abgeben müssten, was zu Gewalt führen könne. Außerdem steige die Bereitschaft Taten anzuzeigen. Haller gab auch zu bedenken, dass nur fünf Prozent der Taten angezeigt würden und das Dunkelfeld deutlich größer sei. Haller: Rechtspraxis muss sich ändern Die Gewaltschutz-Expertin lobte den Einsatz von Bundesjustizministerin Hubig, forderte zugleich aber mehr Präventionsmaßnahmen, Beratungsangebote und Plätze in Frauenhäusern. Auch die Rechtspraxis müsse sich angesichts patriarchaler Gesetzestexte ändern. Man brauche Fortbildungen von Richtern, damit Gewalt gegen Frauen auch erkannt werden könne. Anstieg auch bei digitaler Gewalt Einen Anstieg gab es dem Lagebild des BKA zufolge auch bei digitaler Gewalt. Die Zahl der weiblichen Opfer stieg hier im Vergleich zum Vorjahr um knapp 16 Prozent. Die meisten der 31.221 betroffenen Mädchen und Frauen seien Opfer von Nötigung, Bedrohung und Stalking geworden. Etwa 30 Prozent von ihnen waren demnach zum Tatzeitpunkt minderjährig. Bundestagspräsidentin Klöckner forderte von den Betreibern der Online-Plattformen ein schnelleres Eingreifen. Die CDU-Politikerin schrieb in einem Gastbeitrag für die "Bild"-Zeitung, Hassnachrichten, Drohungen und sexualisierte Fake-Bilder müssten innerhalb von Stunden gelöscht werden. Klöckner verwies darauf, dass sich immer mehr Frauen aus der Öffentlichkeit zurückzögen, sich nicht mehr im Internet äußerten oder darauf verzichteten, für politische Ämter zu kandidieren. Wenn Frauen verstummten, sei das ein gesellschaftliches Problem. Diese Nachricht wurde am 24.11.2026 im Programm Deutschlandfunk gesendet.

title: Führerscheinreform: Lern-Apps, Tempo 60 und digitale Nachweise
subtitle: Rund um den Führerschein stehen in Deutschland mehrere Veränderungen an.
feedText:

articleBody:
Rund um den Führerschein stehen in Deutschland mehrere Veränderungen an. In seiner [1070. Sitzung](https://www.bundesrat.de/SharedDocs/TO/1070/to-node.html) hat der Bundesrat sowohl der Änderung des Fahrlehrergesetzes zugestimmt als auch eine Initiative zur Anhebung der Höchstgeschwindigkeit von Kleinkrafträdern auf den Weg gebracht.

#### Anwesenheitspflicht entfällt: Führerschein-Theorie per App

Parallel dazu bereiten sich erste App-Anbieter auf die veränderten Rahmenbedingungen für die Führerscheinausbildung vor.

Mit der Reform entfällt die Präsenzpflicht beim Theorieunterricht. Fahrschüler sollen sich künftig auch vollständig digital auf ihre theoretische Prüfung vorbereiten können. Ein Großteil der gesetzlichen Änderungen tritt zum 1. Juli 2027 in Kraft.

Zu den Anbietern, die sich bereits jetzt positionieren, gehört das Berliner Unternehmen SAFE. Dessen [gleichnamiges Lernangebot](https://machsafe.de) ist bereits im Web und auf Android-Geräten gestartet. Eine iPhone-App soll demnächst folgen.

#### SAFE will Theorie-Ausbildung per App anbieten

Neben über 1.000 Videos, in denen ein Fahrlehrer die amtlichen Prüfungsfragen erläutert, umfasst das Angebot 64 Videolektionen, Prüfungssimulationen und einen am individuellen Prüfungstermin ausgerichteten Lernplan. [Die Preise](https://machsafe.de/) beginnen bei einmalig 149 Euro. Interessierte können das Angebot sieben Tage kostenlos ausprobieren.

## Bundesrat will Tempo 60 für Kleinkrafträder

Unabhängig von der Führerscheinreform setzt sich der Bundesrat auf Initiative Sachsens für eine [Anpassung der europäischen Fahrzeugvorschriften](https://www.bundesrat.de/drs.html?id=594-26%28B%29) ein. Statt der bislang vorgesehenen bauartbedingten Höchstgeschwindigkeit von 45 km/h sollen Kleinkrafträder und leichte vierrädrige Fahrzeuge der Führerscheinklasse AM künftig bis zu 60 km/h erreichen dürfen.

#### Bald sollen auch kleinere Mopeds die 45 km/h hinter sich lassen dürfen

Die Länder verweisen auf technische Fortschritte bei Bremsen, Fahrwerken und Reifen sowie auf den Mobilitätsbedarf in ländlichen Regionen. Eine direkte Anhebung der zulässigen Geschwindigkeit geht mit dem Beschluss allerdings nicht einher. Zunächst müssen die europäischen Genehmigungsvorschriften geändert werden.

## Digitaler Führerschein zunächst ohne Foto

Noch für Ende November ist unterdessen die [Erweiterung der i-Kfz-App um den digitalen Führerschein](https://www.iphone-ticker.de/i-kfz-app-digitaler-fuehrerschein-kommt-in-drei-wochen-289996/) vorgesehen. Auch hierzu enthält das am Freitag gebilligte Gesetz eine interessante Übergangsregelung: Solange das Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt technisch nicht auf die erforderlichen Lichtbilder zugreifen kann, darf der digitale Führerschein ohne Foto ausgestellt werden. Bei Verkehrskontrollen müssen Nutzer in dieser Übergangsphase zusätzlich ihren Personalausweis oder Reisepass vorlegen.

[★ iPhone-Ticker bei Google bevorzugen ★](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=iphone-ticker.de)

Der Beitrag [Führerscheinreform: Lern-Apps, Tempo 60 und digitale Nachweise](https://www.iphone-ticker.de/fuehrerscheinreform-lern-apps-tempo-60-und-digitale-nachweise-291299/) Wurde zuerst auf [iphone-ticker.de](https://www.iphone-ticker.de) veröffentlicht.

## Free lunches (permalink)

[↗ Primärquelle: pluralistic.net](https://pluralistic.net/2026/11/24/move-fast-break-kings/#come-and-take-it)

An old joke: "Two economists are walking down the sidewalk and one of them points and says, 'Look, there's a $20 bill, right there on the ground!' The other one is dismissive: 'No, if that was a real $20, someone would have picked it up by now.'"

If that joke leaves you scratching your head, then you've been lucky enough to avoid the neoclassical economist's view of the world as a market whose participants, in aggregate, know everything about what people are buying and selling. In that world if there's a "free lunch" – like a $20 bill on the sidewalk – someone will have already taken it.

Likewise, if there's a seller who's priced their goods at $10 and a buyer who's willing to pay $30, there will be an "arbitrageur" who will be shuttling those $10 goods to those $30 customers and pocketing the difference. Give it enough time and either the seller will raise their price to $30, or the buyer will realize they should only be offering $10.

The market will "clear," with everyone getting everything they need in the most efficient way possible, meaning there's no way to improve anyone's position without making someone else worse off:

[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pareto_efficiency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pareto_efficiency)

When markets *don't* behave like this, neoclassicals hunt for "distortions" that prevent the market from performing this continuous balancing trick. "Distortion" is best understood here as a euphemism for "democratic intervention." If you've ever gotten excited about a commonsense policy solution to a serious economic problem (like public grocery stores as a means of addressing food deserts and greedflation), only to see it shot down by economists who use a lot of jargon to "prove" that it can't possibly work, you've experienced how well "distortion" doomerism keeps us from having nice things.

The economist's allergy to distortions is curiously selective. When a company uses its monopoly power to capture its regulators, or bind its workers to silence, or to erect barriers to entry that keep competitors at bay, somehow that doesn't qualify as a "distortion." Same goes for the situation in which a dominant retailer (Walmart) and a dominant manufacturer (Pepsi) come to a secret agreement to force everyone else to raise prices a *ton* so that Walmart can raise its prices by a (smaller) ton and still be "the cheapest":

[https://pluralistic.net/2024/08/14/the-price-is-wright/#enforcement-priorities](https://pluralistic.net/2024/08/14/the-price-is-wright/#enforcement-priorities)

Economists are in love with the idea of the economy as a self-licking ice-cream cone, a beautiful machine that operates all by itself, processing all the information we inject into it by buying and selling and finding the optimal way to produce more of the things we want best at the lowest prices.

But like any love-drunk suitor, economists habitually overlook the market's glaring imperfections. In the self-correcting market, a company with high margins sends up a flare that alerts other, hungrier companies to swarm it, competing to offer the cheapest price. Likewise any company with lots of customers: those crowds of customers should conjure up armies of clever planners and inventors who find more efficient ways to produce the same goods and services and lure those customers away.

This is the crux of market orthodoxy, the idea that competition lowers margins, goading sellers to offer better goods at better prices. Don't take my word for it, here's Adam Smith:

> It is not from the benevolence of the butcher, the brewer, or the baker, that we expect our dinner, but from their regard to their own interest. We address ourselves, not to their humanity, but to their self-love, and never talk to them of our own necessities, but of their advantages.

If this is true, then the surest sign of a "market distortion" is persistent high margins and persistent high market-share. Any company that dominates its market and charges far more than its costs is a crisp, $20 bill lying right there on the sidewalk for all to see. If no one picks up that $20, then it's a sure bet that there's a "distorter" who is preventing the market from acting on the "information" that there is an opportunity here.

America's business lobby *loves* distortions, so long as they're the kinds of distortions that let the companies safely entrust their $20 bills to the sidewalk without worrying about having them scooped up by a competitor.

Take Big Tech: this is an industry with such persistently high margins and so many customers that there are *multiple* firms in the sector that were able to piss away *hundreds of billions of dollars* by manipulating their stock prices with buybacks and building AI data-centers that can never turn a profit:

[https://pluralistic.net/2025/09/06/computer-says-huh/#invisible-handcuffs](https://pluralistic.net/2025/09/06/computer-says-huh/#invisible-handcuffs)

If the market was "undistorted" then anyone this rich and this stupid would be in serious trouble. Ask a neoclassical to explain Big Tech's prolonged, morbid wealth and they'll insist that this means that *we're* the stupid ones, because we can't play 11-dimensional chess like Zuckerberg, which is why we can't understand why it was *good* to piss away $80b on the metaverse.

But we don't have to look very hard to find another, simpler explanation. Big Tech owes its profits to its monopoly power, which allows it to form cartels that collude to rig prices:

[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jedi_Blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jedi_Blue)

Big Tech has so much money that it can capture its regulators, securing favorable laws that make it literally *illegal* to build competing products, so we're all stuck as hostages of the platforms:

[https://pluralistic.net/2026/01/14/sole-and-despotic/#world-turned-upside-down](https://pluralistic.net/2026/01/14/sole-and-despotic/#world-turned-upside-down)

An "undistorted" market is one where information is presumed to flow freely among market participants. But the business lobby has secured far-reaching legal protection for the nondisclosure and noncompete "agreements" it crams down the throats of its workers, customers and suppliers, making it *literally illegal* to warn other people about the defects in both its products and its managers' character:

[https://pluralistic.net/2026/06/27/zuckerstreisand-2/#autodisparagement](https://pluralistic.net/2026/06/27/zuckerstreisand-2/#autodisparagement)

An "undistorted" market is one in which the state intervenes to enforce contracts. Without that intervention, cheaters can beat trustworthy competitors by making promises they have no intention of keeping. Yet, the business lobby has secured government backing for "binding arbitration" waivers that make it illegal to sue people who cheat you, forcing you to have your case heard by a fake judge who works for the cheater and nearly always rules in their favor (and whose rulings are legally secret, so you can't warn others so they don't get cheated as well):

[https://pluralistic.net/2020/04/11/socialized-losses/#justice-restored](https://pluralistic.net/2020/04/11/socialized-losses/#justice-restored)

"Undistorted" markets are supposed to keep firms lean and energetic, forever on the lookout for new ways to attract the best customers and the best workers with the best deals and the best pay. Decades of lax merger enforcement has produced an economy dominated by fat and lazy cartels who substitute bullying and lock-in for innovation and customer service:

[https://www.openmarketsinstitute.org/learn/monopoly-by-the-numbers](https://www.openmarketsinstitute.org/learn/monopoly-by-the-numbers)

The business lobby and their tame economists have invented all kinds of gimmicks to "disprove" your intuition that you're worse off every year thanks to cheaters and their rising profits.

For example, there are plenty of mainstream economists who insist that the wage stagnation that has trapped American workers for decades is a hoax. They point to statistics that show that when you include "transfers," American workers are doing just as well as their foreign counterparts, and in particular, that the American public continues to enjoy healthy levels of "consumption" (buying things).

These are very dodgy stats indeed. Here's how they're calculated: the American consumption figures include the health care received by the American public. That health care includes Medicare payments on behalf of Americans who age out of employer-provided insurance, and Medicaid payments made on behalf of poor Americans. These medical services cost 200-300% more than the same services when provided in other advanced economies (Canada, Germany, the UK, etc).

So when a poor American in Buffalo gets Medicaid dialysis at three times the price of a dialysis session in Toronto, that is counted toward that poor person's consumption levels, as though they had just gone out and spent hundreds of dollars on treats from the Cheesecake Factory and the Apple Store. In reality, they've received an overpriced service (whose costs were absorbed by the public purse). They haven't seen an extra dime to spend on either the necessities of life or a little treat:

[https://capitalisnt.com/episodes/can-capitalism-be-popular-FcXPThM6](https://capitalisnt.com/episodes/can-capitalism-be-popular-FcXPThM6)

America spends more on health-care than any other rich nation, and gets less for its money than anyone else. In other words: neoclassical economists use the sky-high monopoly prices set by America's overpriced, underdelivering health care cartel to claim that we've got tons of "real" income, because they factor in the hundreds of billions in public subsidy the feds and the states funnel to these persistently high-margin (and therefore definitively inefficient) businesses.

Get rid of the statistical mirages and a very different America comes into focus: one in which large businesses have fused with a corrupted state that serves as bagman and enforcer for the corporate sector as it rips off workers and consumers.

Remember the decades when tech bros insisted that their "disruption" was all in service to shattering the death grip that legacy industries had on our economy? Uber's early champions insisted that the taxi sector had been "distorted" by overreaching regulation. Once Uber injected "information" about willing riders and willing drivers into the system, the market would clear, pairing drivers and riders in such a way that no one could be made better off without making someone else worse off. Today, Uber uses its lock-in to pay drivers less and less and charge riders more and more – and Uber uses IP law to prevent competitors from making an app that lets drivers automatically shop for better pay and apps that let riders find cheaper rides:

[https://pluralistic.net/2026/07/11/your-risk/#my-reward](https://pluralistic.net/2026/07/11/your-risk/#my-reward)

Uber's "perfect market" is a government-backed monopoly, reliant on the state to block anyone from reverse-engineering its app or unionizing its workers. That fusion of the corporation and the state funnels billions from drivers and riders to investors.

Amazon's founding principle is best summed up in Jeff Bezos's oft-repeated motto, "Your margin is my opportunity." Today, 51-60% of every sale on Amazon's platform is captured by the platform. AWS, Amazon's cloud service, is no longer its most profitable line of business. Today, Amazon's largest source of profit is the $80b it makes every year from charging for search-placement, extracting bribes from sellers to show you items that cost more than the best match for your query:

[https://pluralistic.net/2026/09/04/cheating-at-fraud/#absentee-rentier](https://pluralistic.net/2026/09/04/cheating-at-fraud/#absentee-rentier)

That's a lot of margin – and a lot of opportunity.

Same goes for Apple: the company's most profitable line of business is the 30% app tax it levies on every payment made using an iPhone or iPad. Apple makes $100b/year charging a 30% commission on payments that cost the company less than 1% to process. That's a *lot* of margin.

Then there's the ad-tech duopoly, Meta/Google. These two companies make so much money in an ad system where they represent both buyers and sellers in marketplaces they operate (where they also buy and sell), that they have hundreds of billions left to blow on AI misadventures:

[https://pluralistic.net/2026/10/19/spying-v-context/#unattributed](https://pluralistic.net/2026/10/19/spying-v-context/#unattributed)

In other words, Big Tech's sidewalk is *covered* in $20 bills, which the US government bans American firms from picking up. But that's *America*. What about the rest of the world?

Well, for 25 years, the US Trade Representative has made it America's business to see to it that every US trading partner enacted laws that protected America's tech companies from competitors. Thus the UK's pavements are littered with 20 pound notes, and the EU's are covered in 20 euro notes:

[https://pluralistic.net/2026/01/01/39c3/#the-new-coalition](https://pluralistic.net/2026/01/01/39c3/#the-new-coalition)

The US Trade Rep used both a carrot and a stick to extract these policy concessions from the rest of the world. The carrot was the promise of tariff-free access to the American consumer (the world's richest, shoppingest, most numerous consumer cohort) – the stick was the threat of tariffs.

Today, the stick is broken and the carrot is gone. The American consumer's wallet has been drained. American homeowners groan under multiple mortgages. American renters give 50% of their paycheck to Wall Street slumlords. The US healthcare system has emptied their bank accounts and student debt came for the rest. When American economists have to use the fact that you're too poor to afford overpriced health-care to "prove" that you're rolling in dough, you know the end is nigh. America's growth industries are "financial services" that let you pay for a burrito in four installments – and gambling. The median American worker has $955 saved for retirement:

[https://pluralistic.net/2026/04/12/always-great/#our-nhs](https://pluralistic.net/2026/04/12/always-great/#our-nhs)

Then there's tariffs: as November Kelly says, "Trump inherited a poker game rigged in his favor and flipped the table over anyway because he resented having to pretend to play." The tariffs Trump imposed on every country in the world (even the uninhabited penguin islands) destroyed tariffs' deterrent value:

[https://pluralistic.net/2025/12/16/k-shaped-recovery/#disenshittification-nations](https://pluralistic.net/2025/12/16/k-shaped-recovery/#disenshittification-nations)

America's tech margins are the world's opportunity. It's time to move fast and break (tech's) things. It's time to move fast and break *kings*. Any economist who truly believes in markets would cheer this on: after all, repealing the "market-distorting" laws the US bound the world to can only increase market efficiency, right? Get rid of trade secrecy, nondisclosure and nondisparagement so that market actors have the information they need to make buy/sell decisions. Get rid of IP laws that block reverse-engineering, scraping and other tactics that facilitate switching to a competitor's service, using your own payment processor, or hijacking and rewriting search results to purge paid placement.

Silicon Valley told us we all have a duty to disrupt sclerotic, top-heavy, lazy industries and treat their margins as our opportunity. When they did it to us, that wasn't progress. If we do it to them, that's not piracy.

It's just business.

title: New laser welding process joins aluminum castings with fewer pores and less spatter
subtitle: Laser welding can now join cast aluminum directly to cast aluminum.
feedText: Producing high-quality joints between aluminum die-cast components has long been a major challenge. Process-related pores and gas inclusions in the material can open during conventional laser beam welding. title: Chinesische Raumfahrt: China will erstmals Ausländer auf Raumstation schicken
subtitle: Zweimal im Jahr tauscht China auf seiner Weltraumstation Tiangong die Crew aus.
feedText: Startseite Astronomie Aktuelle Seite: China will erstmals Ausländer auf Raumstation schicken © China Manned Space Engineering Office (Ausschnitt) Die chinesische Raumstation Tiangong 1 wurde im Jahr 2011 gestartet (Illustration). China wird erstmals einen ausländischen Raumfahrer für einen Kurzaufenthalt auf seine Weltraumstation schicken. Muhammad Zeeshan Ali aus Pakistan werde als sogenannter Nutzlastspezialist mit der Mission »Shenzhou 24« auf die Station Tiangong (deutsch: Himmelspalast) reisen und dort Experimente durchführen, erklärte die chinesische Behörde für bemannte Raumfahrt. Die Mission Shenzhou 24 soll an diesem Mittwoch, den 24. November 2026, um 01:18 Uhr MEZ vom Raketenstartplatz Jiuquan in der nordwestchinesischen Wüste Gobi abheben. Kommandant sei Tang Hongbo, der als erster Taikonaut Chinas zum dritten Mal auf die Tiangong fliegen werde, sagte Behördensprecher Zhang Jingbo in Jiuquan.
articleBody:
# China will erstmals Ausländer auf Raumstation schicken - Spektrum der Wissenschaft

## China will erstmals Ausländer auf Raumstation schicken

Startseite Astronomie Aktuelle Seite: China will erstmals Ausländer auf Raumstation schicken © China Manned Space Engineering Office (Ausschnitt) Die chinesische Raumstation Tiangong 1 wurde im Jahr 2011 gestartet (Illustration). China wird erstmals einen ausländischen Raumfahrer für einen Kurzaufenthalt auf seine Weltraumstation schicken. Muhammad Zeeshan Ali aus Pakistan werde als sogenannter Nutzlastspezialist mit der Mission »Shenzhou 24« auf die Station Tiangong (deutsch: Himmelspalast) reisen und dort Experimente durchführen, erklärte die chinesische Behörde für bemannte Raumfahrt. Die Mission Shenzhou 24 soll an diesem Mittwoch, den 24. November 2026, um 01:18 Uhr MEZ vom Raketenstartplatz Jiuquan in der nordwestchinesischen Wüste Gobi abheben. Kommandant sei Tang Hongbo, der als erster Taikonaut Chinas zum dritten Mal auf die Tiangong fliegen werde, sagte Behördensprecher Zhang Jingbo in Jiuquan. Für Raumfahrer Wu Yi sei es der erste Aufenthalt. Die Shenzhou 24 wird die aktuelle dreiköpfige Crew der Shenzhou 23 auf der chinesischen Raumstation ablösen. Für ihre rund sechs Monate im All sind unter anderem Wartungsarbeiten und 90 Experimente vorgesehen. Neu ist diesmal, dass mit Zhu Yangzhu ein Teammitglied seinen Aufenthalt um weitere sechs Monate verlängert und damit einen Jahresaufenthalt auf der Raumstation absolvieren soll. Bei dem regelmäßigen Crewtausch auf der Tiangong übergeben die Raumfahrer über mehrere Tage die Station an ein neues Team. Den freien Platz in der Rückkehrkapsel der Shenzhou 23 neben Zhang Zhiyuan und der Hongkonger Raumfahrerin Lai Ka-ying (Hochchinesisch: Li Jiaying) soll dann Zeeshan Ali besetzen, der damit schon nach kurzer Zeit zurückkehrt. (dpa/AMü) © dpa/spektrum.de

title: Was Mamdani furious about 'Jesus Is Coming' billboard in Times Square?
subtitle: Posts featuring video of billboards promoting Jesus Christ also circulated in 2025, before Mamdani took office.
feedText: In October and November, several posts claimed advertisements in Times Square featuring Jesus Christ left New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani "furious." A Facebook post shared a video of the advertisement, which reads "Jesus Is Coming." Another post said: Jesus Christ is taking center stage in Times Square, New York City! Images of Jesus appearing on massive digital billboards in the heart of Manhattan are drawing attention, with posts circulating online claiming that Zohran Mamdani is furious over the displays. Regardless of the political controversy surrounding New York City, seeing the image of Christ displayed so prominently in one of the world's most recognizable locations is certainly making a statement. Perhaps New York City isn't as far gone as some people believe!
articleBody:
# Was Mamdani furious about 'Jesus Is Coming' billboard in Times Square?

About this rating

In October and November, several posts claimed advertisements in Times Square featuring Jesus Christ left New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani "furious."

A Facebook post shared a video of the advertisement, which reads "Jesus Is Coming." Another post said:

> Jesus Christ is taking center stage in Times Square, New York City! Images of Jesus appearing on massive digital billboards in the heart of Manhattan are drawing attention, with posts circulating online claiming that Zohran Mamdani is furious over the displays. Regardless of the political controversy surrounding New York City, seeing the image of Christ displayed so prominently in one of the world's most recognizable locations is certainly making a statement. Perhaps New York City isn't as far gone as some people believe!

(Facebook user "Robin Martyr")

There is no evidence Mamdani, who is Muslim, was "furious" over advertisements of Jesus on Times Square billboards. Mamdani has made no such public statement or criticized the promotion of images of Jesus. On the contrary, Mamdani has frequently spoken in favor of religious freedom and diversity. As such, we rate this claim as false.

We searched through Mamdani's recent statements and found no such expression of anger. In fact, in April, Mamdani posted a message for Easter Sunday ( archived ): "Happy Easter, New York! Today, millions of New Yorkers celebrate the resurrection of Jesus Christ and the victory of hope over despair and faith over fear."

A spokesperson for Mamdani told us over email, "There is no truth to this claim."

The footage of the advertisement of Jesus Christ in Times Square previously appeared online ( archived ) in December 2025 — before Mamdani took office — if not earlier.

The claim that Mamdani was furious spread via social media accounts that frequently share unverified information unsupported by reliable media coverage. One such Facebook page, Robyn Martyr , is devoted to pro-Christianity content.

Any company or organization can rent advertising space and time on a Times Square billboard. After Mamdani became mayor, we reported on how the Florida Chamber of Commerce paid for an advertisement in Times Square that appeared to mock him, calling him Florida's "Economic Developer of the Year."

Snopes has covered numerous false rumors about Mamdani .

articleBody:
# BKA-Zahlen 2025: Gewalt gegen Frauen auf neuem Höchststand

## BKA zu häuslicher Gewalt : Gewalt gegen Frauen steigt: Erfasste Übergriffe in Zahlen

Schläge vom Partner, sexuelle Übergriffe oder sogar Mord: Jedes Jahr werden Zehntausende Frauen in Deutschland Opfer von Gewalt. Die Zahl erfasster Übergriffe ist 2025 gestiegen.

Die Bundesregierung und das BKA stellen das Lagebild zu Gewalt an Frauen im Jahr 2025 vor. Bundesjustizministerin Hubig kündigte an, dass Frauen zukünftig besser geschützt werden sollen.

Die Zahl der registrierten Opfer häuslicher Gewalt hat im vergangenen Jahr einen neuen Höchststand erreicht - dabei ist weiterhin die große Mehrheit der Betroffenen weiblich, während die Tatverdächtigen meist männlich sind.

Wie die Bundesregierung und das Bundeskriminalamt an diesem Dienstag mitteilten, wurden 2025 fast 198.000 Fälle gemeldet, in denen Frauen oder Mädchen Opfer häuslicher Gewalt geworden waren. Das waren 2,8 Prozent mehr als im Jahr zuvor.

- Gewalt gegen Frauen : "Ich bin stark femizid-bedroht und meine Kinder auch"
## 342 Frauen und Mädchen tödlich verletzt

Bundesinnenminister Alexander Dobrindt (CSU), Frauen- und Familienministerin Karin Prien (CDU) sowie die stellvertretende BKA-Chefin Martina Link stellten in Berlin die Zahlen zu häuslicher Gewalt sowie zu geschlechtsspezifisch gegen Frauen gerichteten Straftaten vor. Die Berichte beziehen sich zum Teil auf dieselben Zahlen des Bundeskriminalamts, so etwa bei häuslicher Gewalt. Die spezifisch gegen Frauen gerichteten Straftaten gehen aber darüber hinaus.

Insgesamt wurden 342 Frauen und Mädchen tödlich verletzt, davon 209 durch Gewalt in der Partnerschaft oder der Familie, wie das BKA darlegt. 2024 wurden laut Statistik insgesamt 308 getötete Frauen und Mädchen erfasst.

articleBody:
# Geld für den guten Zweck: Vor allem junge Menschen spenden mehr

Die Spendenbereitschaft in Deutschland ist in den ersten neun Monaten des Jahres gestiegen. Wie der Deutsche Spendenrat am Dienstag in Berlin mitteilte, wurden zwischen Januar und September insgesamt 3,2 Milliarden Euro für gemeinnützige Zwecke gespendet. Das sind knapp 149 Millionen Euro oder fünf Prozent mehr als im Vorjahreszeitraum.

## Zahl der Spender rückläufig, aber höhere Einzelbeträge

Grund sind vor allem höhere Einzelbeträge, denn gleichzeitig ging die Zahl der Spender zurück. Während im Vorjahreszeitraum noch rund 13,1 Millionen Menschen Geld für soziale, humanitäre oder gemeinnützige Zwecke gaben, waren es in den ersten neun Monaten dieses Jahres noch 12,4 Millionen. 2025 war das Spendenvolumen noch rückläufig.

Besonders hoch fielen die Summen demnach für örtliche Projekte aus. In diesem Bereich wurden den Angaben zufolge 874 Millionen Euro gesammelt. Auch in der Not- und Katastrophenhilfe kamen 598 Millionen Euro zusammen.

## Jüngere spenden mehr, am meisten Senioren

Der Zuwachs der Gesamtspenden in diesem Jahr geht damit vor allem auf höhere Einzelbeträge zurück. Dem Spendenrat zufolge wurden bis einschließlich September im Schnitt 45 Euro gespendet und damit sechs Prozent mehr als im Vorjahreszeitraum.

Einen besonders deutlichen Spendenzuwachs beobachtete der Spendenrat bei jungen Menschen unter 30 Jahren. Aus dieser Altersgruppe wurden bis September 248 Millionen Euro gespendet. Das entspricht einem Anstieg von rund einem Drittel oder 34 Prozent im Vergleich zum gleichen Zeitraum des Jahres 2025. Bei den 40- bis 59-Jährigen ging das Spendenvolumen jedoch zurück. Die meisten Spenden fließen nach wie vor aus der Gruppe der über 60-Jährigen mit 1,1 Milliarden Euro.

Für die Weihnachtszeit prognostiziert der Deutsche Spendenrat einen Zuwachs von etwa fünf Prozent beim gesamten Spendenaufkommen.

## Bundesweite Tendenz auch in Bayern erkennbar

Auch in Bayern spendeten die Menschen in den ersten neun Monaten dieses Jahres mehr Geld als im Vorjahreszeitraum – und zwar 623,8 Millionen Euro. Von Januar bis September 2025 kamen 617,6 Millionen Euro zusammen.

Auch in Bayern sinkt die Zahl der Spender. 2025 registrierte der Spendenrat noch 2,7 Millionen Spender im Freistaat, dieses Jahr waren es 2,5 Millionen. Die durchschnittliche Summe je Spende stieg von 43 auf 45 Euro. Jeder Spender gab im Schnitt 5,6 Mal Geld für wohltätige Zwecke oder andere Spendenzwecke.

## Auswertung für Dachverband

Die Daten basieren auf einer Auswertung des "Charity Panel" des Marktforschungsunternehmens YouGov im Auftrag des Deutschen Spendenrates. Dafür wurden monatliche schriftliche Angaben auf der Grundlage von 10.000 Panelteilnehmern ausgewertet. Der Deutsche Spendenrat ist ein Dachverband von 80 spendensammelnden, gemeinnützigen Organisationen.

Der Zuwachs der Gesamtspenden in diesem Jahr geht damit vor allem auf höhere Einzelbeträge zurück. Dem Spendenrat zufolge wurden bis einschließlich September im Schnitt 45 Euro gespendet und damit sechs Prozent mehr als im Vorjahreszeitraum.

Einen besonders deutlichen Spendenzuwachs beobachtete der Spendenrat bei jungen Menschen unter 30 Jahren. Aus dieser Altersgruppe wurden bis September 248 Millionen Euro gespendet. Das entspricht einem Anstieg von rund einem Drittel oder 34 Prozent im Vergleich zum gleichen Zeitraum des Jahres 2025. Bei den 40- bis 59-Jährigen ging das Spendenvolumen jedoch zurück. Die meisten Spenden fließen nach wie vor aus der Gruppe der über 60-Jährigen mit 1,1 Milliarden Euro.

Für die Weihnachtszeit prognostiziert der Deutsche Spendenrat einen Zuwachs von etwa fünf Prozent beim gesamten Spendenaufkommen.

## Bundesweite Tendenz auch in Bayern erkennbar

Auch in Bayern spendeten die Menschen in den ersten neun Monaten dieses Jahres mehr Geld als im Vorjahreszeitraum – und zwar 623,8 Millionen Euro. Von Januar bis September 2025 kamen 617,6 Millionen Euro zusammen.

Auch in Bayern sinkt die Zahl der Spender. 2025 registrierte der Spendenrat noch 2,7 Millionen Spender im Freistaat, dieses Jahr waren es 2,5 Millionen. Die durchschnittliche Summe je Spende stieg von 43 auf 45 Euro. Jeder Spender gab im Schnitt 5,6 Mal Geld für wohltätige Zwecke oder andere Spendenzwecke.

## Auswertung für Dachverband

Die Daten basieren auf einer Auswertung des "Charity Panel" des Marktforschungsunternehmens YouGov im Auftrag des Deutschen Spendenrates. Dafür wurden monatliche schriftliche Angaben auf der Grundlage von 10.000 Panelteilnehmern ausgewertet. Der Deutsche Spendenrat ist ein Dachverband von 80 spendensammelnden, gemeinnützigen Organisationen.

Mit Informationen von AFP, epd und dpa

Das ist die Europäische Perspektive bei BR24.

articleBody:
# SAMA: Training-Free Consensus Ridge Tracking for Camera-Based Heart Rate on Five Public Datasets

## Computer Science > Artificial Intelligence

- [Submitted on 20 Nov 2026] Title: SAMA: Training-Free Consensus Ridge Tracking for Camera-Based Heart Rate on Five Public Datasets Authors: Sudhakar Mishra View a PDF of the paper titled SAMA: Training-Free Consensus Ridge Tracking for Camera-Based Heart Rate on Five Public Datasets, by Sudhakar Mishra View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) is usually benchmarked by one heart rate per video, a figure that hides the short windows in which a tele-consultation would actually read the pulse. We present SAMA, a training-free estimator that (i) forms a quality-weighted consensus of POS and CHROM chrominance spectra, (ii) discounts frequencies occupied by pulse-free references derived from the same frames (frame motion, skin-mask geometry and background brightness), (iii) follows the heart rate through time with a Viterbi ridge under a random-walk prior, and (iv) returns a track-filtered, amplitude-normalised waveform with a per-window confidence. No parameter is learned and no dataset-specific tuning is used. On 218 recordings from 111 participants in five public datasets (UBFC-rPPG, PURE, SUMS, M3PD and a two-participant subset of MMPD), all processed with the same fixed face box and scored with a re-implementation of the rPPG-Toolbox protocol, SAMA has the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) averaged over datasets at every protocol level: 4.40 against 5.13,bpm for POS per video, 4.80 against 5.43 on 30,s windows and 5.05 against 6.59 on 10,s windows. Pooled over participants, the bootstrap interval of its paired difference from POS excludes zero on 30,s and 10,s windows (Wilcoxon p=0.11 and 0.004) but not per video, and it does not beat POS on SUMS per video or on the MMPD subset. Withholding the 20\% least confident windows lowers the pooled 10,s error from 4.06 to 2.33,bpm. We also show that the per-video protocol has a floor of 1.2--1.6,bpm on datasets where heart rate drifts, and that skin tone cannot be recovered from uncalibrated video, which motivates the instrumented, skin-tone-stratified collection we propose for the Indian population. The method does not surpass the best published neural networks on UBFC-rPPG; we report where it stands against them without re-running them. # Pharma: Bayer stoppt Vermarktung von Bestseller-Medikament in Deutschland

Pharmawerk von Bayer in Wuppertal: Hier wurde das Mediakment Kerendia entwickelt. Foto: dpa Zusammenfassung Nutzen Sie komprimierte Kernaussagen für maximale Effizienz in Ihrem News-Alltag – verfügbar im H+ Standard Abo. Jetzt für 1 € testen Düsseldorf, Berlin. Die Bayer AG zieht Konsequenzen aus dem Sparkurs bei der Erstattung neuartiger Arzneien in Deutschland . Der Pharmakonzern kündigte am Dienstag an, sein neues Medikament Kerendia Mitte Dezember hierzulande vom Markt zu nehmen. Für das Mittel seien keine wirtschaftlich akzeptablen Erstattungsbeträge durch die Krankenkassen erreicht worden.

Erstmals reagiert damit ein Anbieter aus Deutschland auf den zunehmenden Streit um die Bezahlung von Arzneien durch die Krankenkassen. Bayer verbindet die Rücknahme mit einer scharfen Kritik am Drücken der Preise.

Dies werde dazu führen, dass immer mehr innovative Mittel aus den Forschungslaboren internationaler Pharmakonzerne nicht mehr in Deutschland zur Verfügung stehen werden, sagte Bayer-Cheflobbyist Matthias Berninger dem Handelsblatt.

articleBody:
This moon lamp is a hot Christmas tip from designer Phoebe Watts (see below)

Gingko Design

The *New Scientist* Christmas gift guide is assembled by our crack team of science editors and experts. If you’re struggling for gift ideas, you will find unexpected and ingenious suggestions for amateur astronomers and animal and nature lovers, as well as those fond of food, beauty and puzzles. And surely that covers all of us?

Space reporter Leah Crane recommends the science-themed jigsaws from Nervous System

Nervous System

## Puzzlingly beautiful: a science jigsaw

If you’re looking for a quick and easy jigsaw to breeze through while watching holiday movies, Nervous System puzzles probably aren’t for you. But if you want something that’s part puzzle, part work of art, and that will keep you transfixed for hours, they’ll definitely do the trick. Nervous System makes laser-cut wooden puzzles with uniquely shaped pieces and science themes, and they are absolutely beautiful. I’m particularly a fan of their geode puzzles, featuring concentric wiggles of bright colour, including wiggly sides that defy every puzzler’s instinct to start with the edge pieces. For even more of a challenge, they make infinity puzzles that can be assembled and reassembled many different ways – those have no edge pieces at all, and some don’t even have a picture on them! Nervous System also sells absolutely stunning jewellery, lamps and sculptures, but to me the puzzles are the real show-stoppers.

*[Nervous System puzzles](https://n-e-r-v-o-u-s.com/shop/line.php?code=12), from $45* *(£32)*

**Leah Crane**

The CL Companion 8×30 binoculars, as recommended by senior editor Chelsea Whyte

Swarovski Optik

## Zoom in: splashing out on binoculars

The eccentric filmmaker Werner Herzog famously declared that he travels with only a second set of underwear, a map, a toothbrush and a set of binoculars. I don’t travel quite so lightly, but on my next trip, I definitely want to add a pair of nice binos to my baggage. I tested out three sets at varying price levels, taking them down to my favourite spot on my local river and out to my backyard during a clear night with a half-moon overhead. The Nikon Prostaff P3 8×42 binoculars are extremely well balanced and were the most comfortable in my hands. They were particularly well-suited for twilight and brighter. The other Nikon set I tried was the Stabilised 12×25 S, which is much more compact. For my small hands that was fine, and the stabilisation was marvellous at reducing any shaking, both while looking at something fixed like the moon or moving quickly to track an eagle fishing for dinner. The stabilisation requires batteries, so these are probably best – suited to the more prepared adventurer. The stand – out pair was the CL Companion 8×30 from Swarovski Optik. I’ve never seen anything look better than they did through these lenses. They let in an enormous amount of light, making the world look like the brightness has been turned up. And the moon’s craters looked stunningly crisp. For the birdwatcher, wildlife lover or stargazer in your life, these would be a worthwhile, although pretty major, splurge.

[Nikon Prostaff P3 8×42](https://www.nikon.co.uk/en_GB/product/sport-optics/binoculars/prostaff-p3-8x42?srsltid=AYCX9vLs5ncI6HPlo5sBgjGvJMpg-fwoIXxVhpKnBpAwPs2nALhePgBl) *, £159*

[Nikon Stabilised 12×25 S](https://www.nikon.co.uk/en_GB/product/sport-optics/binoculars/stabilized-12x25-BAA951WA?srsltid=AYCX9vIQO-5VpLRqqZa1k-oTWDWJxcoA0T9NmHmL3efXmO7iqSY_WY8e) *, £729*

[CL Companion 8×30 from Swarovski Optik](https://www.swarovskioptik.com/gb/en/outdoor/products/binoculars/clc?gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=142839797&gbraid=0AAAAADuZMWsTJfg7C3tdkNR3WEGyQnHhN&gclid=CjwKCAiA5Y_YBhBbEiwAK5Dl7Xg1oKi9uHrtavOf8IoNM3VkIv16Ry6Udy-K-JyvO9EZp_jBA61RRxoChEIQAvD_BwE) *, from £1070*

**Chelsea White**

Podcast editor Rowan Hooper’s tip this Christmas: the Magenta 5 bat detector

Widcare

## Sounds good: a bat detector

Thomas Nagel’s famous 1974 essay, “What is it like to be a bat?”, argued that we can never fully know the experience of being a bat (or any other animal). I have been testing that argument with my fantastic bat detector. The device picks up on the ultrasound frequencies emitted by bats as they fly overhead and converts them into clicks that we can hear. It also displays the frequency of the squeak, and that allows us to identify the species. In my London back garden I get mostly pipistrelles, our smallest bat at just 4 grams. Nagel is right – I don’t know what it is like to fly and catch moths by echolocation. But it is quite thrilling to hear the clicks as a bat swoops past in the dark, and that experience has got me a little closer to appreciating what it is like to be a bat. There are several options available, but I used the Magenta 5 bat detector from Wildcare.

*[Magenta 5 bat detector](https://www.wildcare.co.uk/bat-detector-starter-kit-10-to-bct.html), £105*

**Rowan Hooper**

Editor Catherine de Lange recommends the Timeshifter app

Natee Meepian/Timeshifter

## Time for bed: a jet lag app

If you have a jetsetter in your life, they are probably by definition the kind of person who is tricky to find a gift for. So why not gift them something money can’t buy (well, almost): an end to jet lag? Many moons ago, I was on a journalism fellowship about sleep at Harvard Medical School, when I visited the lab of sleep scientist Steven Lockley. I was fascinated by his experiments, including work he was doing with NASA astronauts, which looked at circadian rhythms, sleep and what happens when our bodies are out of sync with the natural rhythms of the day. Aside from astronauts, many of us who remain earthbound can still feel these effects – especially those who do regular shift work or long-distance travel. What’s more, a body clock that’s out of whack can have serious health consequences.

I followed Lockley’s research closely over the years, and he was generous enough, whenever I travelled back to Boston, to make me a tailored jet-lag plan – when to sleep or nap in the days before and during my flight, as well as when to wear sunglasses and drink caffeine, all based on what time my flight was and the time difference. Fast forward about a decade, and this service is no longer a personal one – Lockley has created an app called Timeshifter, which allows users to plug in their flight details and instantly receive a step-by-step plan to minimise jet lag. There’s a version of the app for shift workers, too.

I recently tried it on a trip to New York, purchasing a one-off plan rather than the subscription, and I can honestly say that I barely felt any jet lag at all – while my husband was falling asleep in his sushi at dinner.

*[Timeshifter app](https://www.timeshifter.com/), $6.99/month or $69.99/year* *(£5.30/month or £53/year)*

**Catherine de Lange**

Environment reporter Madeleine Cuff recommends the Motus Strength II trainers

Vivobarefoot

## Strong feet: barefoot trainers

Forget spin classes and aerobics – fitness these days is all about strength over heart rate. If a loved one has started talking about “Lifting PBs” and “protein-maxxing”, you could do much worse than getting them some proper footwear for their gym trips. There’s emerging evidence to suggest barefoot trainers strengthen foot muscles compared with regular trainers, including the small, stabilising muscles that improve balance. Vivobarefoot’s Motus Strength are specifically designed for weightlifting sessions – I’ve been wearing them to the gym for the last few weeks and am a total convert. You can also get barefoot shoes for hiking and trail running, for those who prefer the great outdoors to the weights floor.

*[Vivobarefoot Motus Strength](https://www.vivobarefoot.com/uk/explore-motus-strength), £150*

**Madeleine Cuff**

Video editor Emily Bates is enjoying these animal trading cards

Life TGC

## Collect them all: animal trading cards

If, like me, you grew up collecting Pokémon cards but now shudder at the prices and scalpers, there’s a brilliant alternative, and it’s science-themed. Life TCG lets players collect, trade and play using cards based on real-world creatures, with gameplay reminiscent of Top Trumps. But the artwork is the real highlight, a charming mix of realistic paintings, quirky cartoons and special-edition photography. One of my first packs even revealed a stunning South Chinese tiger card (one of my favourite animals). The gameplay itself is fairly simple, but the cards are beautiful enough to work as collectible art pieces in their own right. Better still, first-edition holographic cards are genuinely rare. Each is printed in numbers matching that animal’s estimated population in the wild. Life TCG also donates a portion of its profits to WWF. Collecting cards that look great, teach you something and support wildlife conservation? That’s a rare win.

*[Life TCG cards](https://www.lifetcg.com/?srsltid=AYCX9vIgkCrMBxN3AMeCCMC8brS0E91kw0vWmJpdMIkyh1UXrpdnrX67), from £15*

**Emily Bates**

## Cheers: a guide to the glories of wine

For more than 8000 years (in between struggling to survive), humans have been harvesting and fermenting grapes to make the delicious liquid we call wine. Over that time, we’ve amassed more knowledge about this plant-based product than any other – except the secrets of what gives a wine its distinctive quality. *Noble Nine* is a state-of-the-art guide to that quest and many other things vinous by researcher Andrew Wood – perhaps the only academic anywhere lucky enough to do a PhD in the biology of wine quality. Our first metaphorical glass comes from the merlot wine grape, and we cheerfully drink our way through the other eight in Wood’s selection, including chenin blanc, pinot noir, shiraz, and ending up with sauvignon blanc. Cheers, everyone!

*[Noble Nine: The story and science of the world’s favourite wines](https://granta.com/products/noble-nine/) by Andrew Wood, £20*

**Liz Else**

Fresh herbs will be a regular treat with the AUK Mini 2.0 indoor herb garden, says Madeleine Cuff

AUK

## Herbs on tap: an indoor herb garden

I’ve got a little herb garden outside on my patio, and there’s no better feeling during the warmer months than popping out to fetch some fresh coriander or basil midway through dinner prep. But in the winter, I usually rely on plastic packets of supermarket herbs, which inevitably wilt in the fridge before I use them all. The solution? An indoor herb garden that lets you grow fresh herbs all year round. I’ve tested a few models, and the Auk Mini 2 is the winner for easy setup, stylish design and bountiful harvest. It fits on a shelf in my kitchen and costs about 50p per week to run.

*[Auk Mini 2](https://www.auk.com/), £209*

**Madeleine Cuff**

The Bambu Lab A1 mini 3D Printer, as recommended by Catherine de Lange’s ten-year-old son

Bambu Lab

## Make your own: a 3D printer

For my son’s 10th birthday, his grandmother wanted to gift him a very extravagant present – a 3D printer. I wasn’t convinced at first, worried it would be too big for the house, too technical, dangerous (who wants to let their kids play with melting plastic?) and generally a bad idea. A few months in, I’m happy to be recommending this as a great present for a very special young person in your life. We went for the Bambu Labs A1 mini, which is small enough to be stored out of sight and brought out for supervised use. So far, it’s been very easy to “plug and play”, and my son has printed a range of plastic tat that nobody needed, and a couple of “gifts” for me, including a stand for my phone while I cook (how thoughtful!). Now that we’ve grasped the basics, the next step is for him to learn to design his own projects, which is where things become more educational. I’m also hoping we can use it to print spare parts when appliances break at home. Unlike toys that get played with a few times and forgotten, a 3D printer is a gift that can evolve with your child’s abilities and get used for years to come.

*[Bambu Labs A1 mini 3D printer](https://uk.store.bambulab.com/products/a1-mini?from=navigation), £139*

**Catherine de Lange**

A voucher for a sound bath like this one is features editor Olivia Goldhill’s top tip for a Christmas gift

Emra Sound Healing

## Sound choice: a sound bath voucher

Feeling yourself immersed in the deep vibrations of a singing bowl isn’t just a pleasant acoustic experience. Sound baths – when you listen, usually while lying down, to acoustic instruments –are deeply, deeply relaxing. Studies have found the experience helps [reduce feelings](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fpmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2Farticles%2FPMC5871151%2F&data=05%7C02%7CAlison.Flood%40newscientist.com%7C7553349a2def49ca6a4d08df4490bdfc%7C0f3a4c644dc54a768d4152d85ca158a5%7C0%7C0%7C639305060617198485%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=3Kie1taH4rx4MVxcwZfrey%2Fl4MH%2B%2FKUYWupGcoDZZC4%3D&reserved=0) of anxiety and tension, and there’s also [evidence](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fpmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov%2Farticles%2FPMC12063014%2F&data=05%7C02%7CAlison.Flood%40newscientist.com%7C7553349a2def49ca6a4d08df4490bdfc%7C0f3a4c644dc54a768d4152d85ca158a5%7C0%7C0%7C639305060617228366%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=nf8uAseWRgRxi6dFnH3RNHPm2TN%2Fuzp5ijlGeJpYKdQ%3D&reserved=0) they can improve both sleep and cognitive function. Sound baths are a meditative practice and that, for me, is where the true benefits lie. Silent meditation is difficult, and it’s hard not to grow frustrated with myself for my wandering thoughts and inability to focus on my breath. The beautiful music of sound baths provides an external, soothing distraction. They provide a space to pause and allow to-do lists to gently fade away. There are both private and group-class sound baths, either of which would make a thoughtful gift as a shared activity or simply a new year’s reset.

Sound bath vouchers, from £25 (A few options in [London](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Femrasoundhealing.com%2Fgift-vouchers%2F&data=05%7C02%7CAlison.Flood%40newscientist.com%7C7cd32c0d27364d4a3bfb08df4569fd33%7C0f3a4c644dc54a768d4152d85ca158a5%7C0%7C0%7C639305993655401702%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=kpE1jCIeYmvHkz5xZ3zbuIA2Nl4aMt13FAkHMfnoVmY%3D&reserved=0), [Brighton](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.brightonsound.co.uk%2F&data=05%7C02%7CAlison.Flood%40newscientist.com%7C7cd32c0d27364d4a3bfb08df4569fd33%7C0f3a4c644dc54a768d4152d85ca158a5%7C0%7C0%7C639305993655431921%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=Q9LPnMMNqT84OI7g6ZDeMoEcvwmuNOQw8Ii3kJOOBz0%3D&reserved=0) & [Manchester](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.eventbrite.co.uk%2Fe%2Fthe-new-year-reset-sound-bath-at-the-monastery-manchester-tickets-2002585876264%3Faff%3Debdssbdestsearch%26dsrp_sid%3Dc6be633f-6845-461b-8940-01ef22480b32%26dsrp_item_id%3D2002585876264%26_gl%3D1*kui3d6*_up*MQ..*_ga*NjM0MDg0NjAwLjE3OTUwMDI0NDg.*_ga_TQVES5V6SH*czE3OTUwMDI0NDgkbzEkZzAkdDE3OTUwMDI0NDgkajYwJGwwJGgwJGR3V0hEdTJZLUQxd2xzSTFQeU55a0RBOVZpMC12N2RNcFJR&data=05%7C02%7CAlison.Flood%40newscientist.com%7C7cd32c0d27364d4a3bfb08df4569fd33%7C0f3a4c644dc54a768d4152d85ca158a5%7C0%7C0%7C639305993655455582%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=GfJHwRrAb%2Byt5k58EsO5VgeShc804zB4nmXtrqjqGZY%3D&reserved=0))

**Olivia Goldhill**

Head of books Alison Flood is recommending this guide to surviving the apocalypse

## Disaster ready: a guide to rebuilding civilisation

A regular topic of conversation when I get together with my wider family is how we would survive in the event of an apocalypse, and who would contribute what skills. With my husband an engineer, my brother-in-law a doctor and my mum a brilliant gardener, we think we’d do pretty well, but I’ve decided the key thing I’d contribute is my copy of *The Book*. Subtitled “the ultimate guide to rebuilding civilization”, it covers everything from making fire and beer to leathercraft and traps. Running to 400 pages, it was written with the scientific and technical advice of Lewis Dartnell at the University of Westminster, UK, and would be a fun and practical gift for anyone in your life who is eyeing the future with trepidation.

[The Book](https://hungryminds.com/en-gb/products/the-book) *, £99*

**Alison Flood**

Rowan Hooper also recommends this mushroom growing kit from Merryhill Mushrooms

Merryhill Mushrooms

## Grow your own: a mushroom-growing kit

It is widely accepted that growing your own fruit and vegetables is not only mentally rewarding, but that the food tastes especially good when the gap between picking it and eating it is minimised. But, I thought, what about mushrooms? To find out, I grew my own mushrooms with foolproof growing kits from [Merryhill Mushrooms](http://www.merryhill-mushrooms.co.uk). Choose the species of mushroom, and the company delivers the kit to your door. I tried regular chestnut mushrooms and the impressive lion’s mane mushroom. You really don’t have to do much other than keep their box humid; within a couple of weeks, the mushrooms had emerged from the mycelial mass, and I had picked and eaten them. Mushroom steaks and “pulled shroom” curry. Delicious!

*[Mushroom growing kit](https://www.merryhill-mushrooms.co.uk/) from Merryhill Mushrooms, from £18.95*

**Rowan Hooper**

Designer Phoebe Watts loves the moon lamp she splurged on

Gingko Design

## Lunar magic: a moon lamp

Last year, I stumbled upon the Space store in the Oxford covered market, drawn in by the floating, spinning globes in the window display. The thing that particularly caught my eye was a true 3D-printed model of the moon, suspended by a magnet – it looked like it defied gravity. I subsequently splashed out and bought it! It’s now a great addition to my desk and has become something I really love. The model is raised so that the surface is textured, and you can interact with it a bit. The globe also has three light tones (warm, cool and neutral), which is great for setting a mood. You can get it slightly cheaper elsewhere but if you can, I would highly suggest supporting the Space store. And if this one can’t be justified, they have many other cool products and globe lights that don’t float.

*[Smart moon lamp](https://www.spacestore.co/product/smart-moon-lamp/), £159*

**Phoebe Watts**

Madeleine Cuff has another Christmas tip: CleanOil’s green beauty products

Raven Botanicals

## Green pampering: innovative body oil

Vegetable oils are in almost everything, from beauty products and sandwiches to even pet food. But producing them requires a huge amount of land, energy and water. Clean Food Group is an exciting British company working to change that, using precision fermentation to produce oils from yeast in vats. It estimates its CleanOil product offers a 90 per cent cut to carbon emissions compared with using palm oil. Scottish beauty company Raven Beauty became the first company to use CleanOil in consumer products this year, releasing a facial cleanser in September, [which I road-tested for a New Scientist video](https://eur02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.instagram.com%2Freel%2FDdKHiH9FIbp%2F&data=05%7C02%7CAlison.Flood%40newscientist.com%7C063394402c354779f8c208df33748209%7C0f3a4c644dc54a768d4152d85ca158a5%7C0%7C0%7C639286247638318007%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=0msM5RY5lEMuIG0rJzxmI%2BPGKOgr9Yj4eFZjnJnr65M%3D&reserved=0). Now Raven has released a range of body oils also featuring CleanOil, which would make a great gift for someone who deserves a bit of pampering. Plus, I think this small company deserves a cheer for being one of the first in line for pioneering green technology.

*[Body oil](https://ravenbotanicals.com/collections/body-oils), £38*

**Madeleine Cuff**

Catherine de Lange also recommends this book as a personalised Christmas gift

Fact and Story

## Pinning you down: Your life in data

We may be used to talking about how many times around the sun we have travelled each birthday. But for the inquisitive-minded, there’s more detail to be had. Have you stopped to consider, for instance, how many volcanoes have erupted since the day you were born, or how many times your heart has beaten? How many dinosaurs were named in that time, or elements discovered?

This is the premise behind *Days of You*, a beautiful and personalised hardback book, packed full of data specifically tailored to a specific person. All you have to do is provide the name, date of birth and place of birth of your special someone, and the team behind *Days of You* (which, incidentally, is the brainchild of former *New Scientist* staffer Matt Walker) pulls together stats and data ranging from the shape of the moon on the birthday in question to what the price of tea and the best-selling album were that year. This is essentially a beautifully visualised piece of data journalism, where the subject is your lucky recipient.

It may sound simple, but much of the data is hard to come by – especially from some of the weather stations – and must be tailored to the birth location in question. For that reason, the book is only available for those born in the US and the UK.

Books usually take 5-6 working days from order to door, the team say s, but to be sure, they recommend ordering by 10 December. They also make personalised calendars, mugs, and prints for new babies.

[The Days of You](https://thedaysofyou.com/) *, £49*

**Catherine de Lange**

The Brick physical app blocker – as recommended by Madeleine Cuff

Brick

## Distraction blocker: a Brick tile

Teenagers usually come in for the most scrutiny over phone use, but the truth is we could all do with cutting back on our screen time, no matter our age. Have a chat with your nearest and dearest about their New Year’s resolutions and see if reducing their phone use comes up. If it does, a Brick might be the perfect gift this Christmas. It’s a small magnetic tile, and when you tap your phone against it, a pre-selected group of apps is blocked from use until you tap again. I use mine to curb scrolling during work hours and reduce my phone use around my children at the weekend. I’ve found the extra effort it takes to go and find the Brick to tap and unlock your apps has been enough to rewire my behaviour pretty significantly. Brick has also just launched Brick Night, which blocks selected apps from being used when you enter your bedroom – perfect for preventing doomscrolling before bed.

[Brick](https://getbrick.com/) *, £49, Brick Night, £119*

**Madeleine Cuff**

articleBody:
Airports are places of departures and arrivals, but what happens to those who never seem to leave? At Terminal 1 of Madrid-Barajas Airport, a bronze man sits quietly, apparently waiting for a flight that may never come. Known as El Vagamundos (The Wanderer), this 1996 sculpture by Spanish artist Casto Solano captures the peculiar feeling of being suspended between destinations.

The seated figure has acquired a life of its own through local folklore. Some people believe it commemorates those who have turned airport terminals into temporary homes, stranded by immigration bureaucracy or personal circumstances. One popular story connects the sculpture to a Cuban traveller who allegedly spent 18 months wandering around Barajas in 1992 while trying to secure permission to return to his homeland.

Whether or not the legend is true, El Vagamundos perfectly embodies the strange limbo of airport life: the endless waiting, the transient encounters, and the feeling of belonging nowhere and everywhere at once. Among hurried passengers dragging their suitcases, this traveller has nowhere else to be.

articleBody:
# Altersvorsorgedepot: Banken werben schon, der Staat lässt wohl auf sich warten

## Altersvorsorgedepot: Banken legen los – doch der Staat verspätet sich

Banken und Versicherer werben bereits um Kunden für das neue Altersvorsorgedepot. Doch ausgerechnet die staatliche Alternative lässt auf sich warten: Sie soll frühestens im Sommer 2027 starten.

Während sich Banken und Versicherer schon eine Werbeschlacht um das neue Altersvorsorgedepot liefern, werden Verbraucher noch länger auf die staatliche Variante warten müssen. Eigentlich sieht die neue Form der staatlich geförderten privaten Altersvorsorge vor, dass nicht nur Broker und Banken das neue Produkt anbieten. Auch der Staat sollte ein Altersvorsorgedepot auflegen.

Wie das Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland (RND) berichtet, wird das staatliche Depot aber zum Start am 1. Januar nicht zur Verfügung stehen. Aus Regierungskreisen heißt es, mit der Einführung sei frühestens im Sommer 2027 zu rechnen. Grund für die Verzögerung ist, dass die Verordnung für das öffentlich organisierte Angebot länger dauert als gedacht.

Die Rechtsverordnung muss auch noch festlegen, welche Institution das Angebot verwalten soll. Im Gespräch sind unter anderem Bundesbank, KfW und Deutsche Rentenversicherung. Das Gesetz zum Altersvorsorgedepot ist seit Ende Mai in Kraft.

title: KI im Schulalltag: Immer mehr Lehrkräfte fühlen sich zur Nutzung gedrängt – und fürchten zusätzliche Arbeitsbelastung
subtitle: Künstliche Intelligenz gehört längst zum Berufsalltag vieler Lehrkräfte.
