articleBody:
**Die Tekton T und Tekton Floyd sind zwei Vertreterinnen der im Herbst vorgestellten Tekton-Serie von PRS Guitars.** **Eine Gitarrenlinie, die der amerikanische Hersteller deutlich an die neue Generation moderner Player richtet: ein schlankes Halsprofil mit flacherem Griffbrett, ein leichter Korpus und zwei Humbucker-Pickups, für High-Gain-Einsätze konzipiert, aber auch mit Variationsmöglichkeiten durch Coil-Splitting. Wir haben uns die beiden Gitarren näher angesehen, ihre Möglichkeiten erkundet und herausgefunden, worin sie sich unterscheiden.**

Unser Fazit:

5 / 5

Pro

- ausgezeichnete Verarbeitung
- perfekte werkseitige Voreinstellung
- hervorrangende Bespielbarkeit
- klangliche Variationen mit Coil-Splitting
- Pickups – transparenter Sound auch bei höheren Zerrgraden

Contra

- keins

[Jetzt kaufen Für 2.999,00€ bei](https://www.thomann.de/de/prs_tekton_t_imperial_topaz.htm?offid=1&affid=84)

## PRS Guitars Tekton Series – Das Wichtigste in Kürze

- Was ist die PRS Guitars Tekton Series? Die Gitarren aus der Tekton-Serie sind für den modernen Player konzipiert: schlanker Hals mit D-Shape, etwas flacheres Griffbrett und zwei Humbucker mit transparentem Ton auch bei High-Gain-Sounds.
- Welche Hölzer werden bei der PRS Guitars Tekton T für den Korpus verwendet? Die Tekton T hat einen Mahagoni-Korpus mit einer Mango-Decke und kommt wie alle Gitarren aus der Tekton-Serie mit einem Offset-Double-Cutaway-Korpus, der etwas dünner ist als bei den Standard PRS Modellen.
- Welche Hölzer wurden bei der PRS Guitars Tekton Floyd für den Korpus verwendet? Der Korpus der Tekton Floyd besteht aus Erle.
- Aus welchen Hölzern sind die Hälse der PRS Guitars Tekton Series-Gitarren gefertigt? Alle Instrumente aus der Tekton-Serie sind mit einem Ahornhals (Modern D-Shape) und einem Ebenholzgriffbrett bestückt.
- Welche Pickups sind bei den PRS Guitars Tekton Series Gitarren eingebaut? Die Gitarren sind mit den neu designten Stylus-Humbuckern ausgestattet – ein Stylus T am Steg und ein Stylus B an der Halsposition.
- Gibt es zusätzliche elektronische Optionen? Ja, die Tonabnehmer können per Push/Pull-Funktion des Tonreglers gesplittet werden.
- Welche Hardware ist bei der PRS Guitars Tekton T im Einsatz? Bei der Tekton T wird ein neu entwickeltes Tremolosystem verwendet, das mit Zweipunktbefestigung und Messingsätteln ausgestattet ist.
- Welches Tremolosystem hat die PRS Guitars Tekton Floyd? Bei der Tekton Floyd wird ein Original Floyd Rose 1000 Series Tremolo-System benutzt, mit Klemmsattel und Feinstimmern.
- Wird die Gitarre mit Koffer oder Gigbag ausgeliefert? Die Gitarren der Tekton Series werden alle mit einem Premium-Gigbag ausgeliefert.
- Das sagt der Test: Die PRS Tekton-Modelle verbinden moderne Bespielbarkeit mit klanglicher Vielseitigkeit. Sie überzeugen durch erstklassige Verarbeitung, perfekte Werkseinstellung und transparente Stylus-Pickups, die ihre Stärken besonders bei High-Gain-Sounds ausspielen.

## Was sind die besonderen Eigenschaften der PRS Guitars Tekton Series?

Diverse Kundenwünsche nach einem Gitarrenmodell mit modernen Spezifikationen bildeten den Ausgangspunkt für das Team von PRS Guitars, das auf dieser Basis die Tekton-Serie umsetzte.

Aktuell gibt es vier unterschiedliche Modelle: Tekton (Fixed Bridge), Tekton T (Tremolo), Tekton Floyd (Floyd-Rose-Tremolo), Tekton SVN (Seven String mit 26,5″ Mensur). Alle Gitarren kommen mit einem Doublecut-Korpus, bei dem die Cutaway-Hörner etwas länger sind als beim Standard-PRS-Shaping. Außerdem ist der Korpus minimal dünner, was sich im geringeren Gewicht positiv bemerkbar macht. Der Hals-Korpus-Übergang ist ergonomisch geformt, sodass die hohen Lagen sehr gut erreichbar sind. Stichwort Hals: Der schlanke D-Shape-Hals aus Ahorn ist mit einem Ebenholz-Griffbrett mit 16″-Radius und 24 Edelstahl-Jumbo-Bünden bestückt. Für die Tekton-Modelle wurden auch die neuen Stylus-Pickups entwickelt, deren Fokus auf High-Gain-Sounds liegt, mit klarem Ton und sauberer Saitentrennung.

## In welcher Qualität sind die verwendeten Bauteile?

Die PRS Guitars Tekton T und Tekton Floyd sind hervorragend verarbeitet – genau so, wie man es von PRS-USA-Modellen gewohnt ist. Stimmmechaniken und beide Tremolosysteme arbeiten einwandfrei, lediglich den einen oder anderen könnten die mitschwingenden Federn bei harten High-Gain-Einsätzen etwas stören.

Die Pickups übertragen erstklassig, allerdings auch kleine Nebengeräusche. Die fallen bei mittleren Zerrgraden zwar nicht wirklich auf, aber wenn der Gain-Regler weit oben steht, treten sie ans Tageslicht. Aber dafür gibt es ja einfache Abhilfe in Form von Gummiringen (String Dampener).

## Wie ist die Einstellung der PRS Guitars Tekton Series ab Werk?

An der Einstellung von Hals und Saitenlage gibt es nichts zu kritisieren. Die Halsneigung sowie das Abrichten und Polieren der Bünde sind akkurat erledigt. Beide Gitarren kommen mit moderater, nicht allzu flacher Saitenlage, die schnarrfreies Spielen erlaubt.

## Entspricht das Angebot dem Preis?

Beide Gitarren liegen preislich in der Oberklasse um 3000 Euro und die Lieferung entspricht den Erwartungen: Hervorragende Verarbeitung, Holz-Abstimmung und dadurch resultierendes Schwingungsverhalten, erstklassige Bespielbarkeit und die Sounds, die von den Stylus-Pickups übertragen werden, rechtfertigen den Preis.

articleBody:
Ukrainian explosive naval drones sank a Russian warship docked in the port city of Benghazi in Libya while also striking a Russian cargo ship that it was escorting. The incident demonstrates the expanding scope of Ukrainian military strikes on Russian ships from the coast of North Africa to the Gulf of Finland.

The Russian Navy’s [missile corvette Merkury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_corvette_Merkury) sank at port after being struck by at least two Ukrainian naval drones on November 22, according to the [Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/libya-russia-ukriane-war-benghazi-ship-drone-cbd82b965a111dcf4605b8b2d0493780). Ukraine’s Security Service described using seven naval drones launched from a mother ship to target the *Merkury*, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy [shared video footage](https://x.com/ZelenskyyUa/status/2124764825049850041) showing the drone boats approaching and exploding against both the burning Russian warship and a Russian dry cargo ship, *MV Angara*.

Zelenskyy noted that a Ka-27 combat helicopter onboard the *Merkury* was also destroyed. He described the cargo ship *MV Angara* as transporting weapons—Russia provides material support to the Libyan National Army that currently controls Benghazi and is battling the internationally recognized Libyan government based in Tripoli.

title: Pessimismus statt Aufschwung: Warum neun von zehn Firmen für 2027 keine Erholung erwarten
subtitle: Während offizielle Prognosen ein Comeback der Konjunktur ankündigen, überwiegt in den Betrieben die Skepsis: 90 Prozent der Firmen erwarten 2027 keine Erholung.
feedText: Während offizielle Prognosen ein Comeback der Konjunktur ankündigen, überwiegt in den Betrieben die Skepsis: 90 Prozent der Firmen erwarten 2027 keine Erholung.
articleBody:
# Umfrage: Neun von zehn Firmen erwarten 2027 keine Erholung

- Startseite
- Wirtschaft
## Pessimismus statt Aufschwung: Warum neun von zehn Firmen für 2027 keine Erholung erwarten

Stand: 24.11.2026, 13:24 Uhr

Von: Patrick Huljina

Kommentare Drucken Teilen

Während offizielle Prognosen ein Comeback der Konjunktur ankündigen, überwiegt in den Betrieben die Skepsis: 90 Prozent der Firmen erwarten 2027 keine Erholung.

Zwischen den mathematischen Modellrechnungen der Wirtschaftsforschung und der Einschätzung in den Chefetagen klafft eine deutliche Differenz. Während die EU-Kommission und auch die Wachstumsprognosen der Institute für das laufende Jahr von einem Wachstum von 1,3 Prozent nach vorangegangener Stagnation ausgehen, zeichnen die Unternehmen ein anderes Bild: Neun von zehn Firmen in Deutschland rechnen für das kommende Jahr 2027 mit einer anhaltenden Konjunkturflaute statt mit einer nachhaltigen Erholung.

Das geht aus einer im Oktober durchgeführten Zusatzbefragung des arbeitgebernahen Instituts der deutschen Wirtschaft (IW Köln) unter 935 Unternehmen hervor, über die die Zeitungen der Funke Mediengruppe berichten. Eine spürbare Trendwende zum Besseren erwartet die überwältigende Mehrheit der Betriebe demnach im nächsten Jahr nicht.

## Gedämpfte Erwartungen in der Industrie: Kaum Hoffnung auf rasche Wende

Besonders skeptisch fällt das Stimmungsbild im industriellen Kern der deutschen Wirtschaft aus. Im verarbeitenden Gewerbe glauben nach den IW-Zahlen lediglich sechs Prozent der Firmen an eine konjunkturelle Wende im kommenden Jahr. Ähnlich zurückhaltend beurteilt das Baugewerbe die Perspektiven, in dem nur sieben Prozent mit einer spürbaren Belebung rechnen. Im Dienstleistungssektor blicken zwölf Prozent der Betriebe positiv nach vorn.

Die Ergebnisse decken sich mit dem Trend regionaler Erhebungen der vergangenen Monate. Auch in Hessen zeigte sich in den Befragungen der Industrie- und Handelskammern eine große Skepsis in regionalen Betrieben : Bei einer Umfrage der IHK Frankfurt unter rund 2000 Mitgliedsunternehmen rechnete knapp ein Drittel mit einer weiteren Eintrübung der Geschäfte und nur zwölf Prozent mit Besserung, während viele Betriebe ihre Investitionsbudgets kürzen.

## Hohe Energiekosten und Arbeitsbelastung als Hauptbremsen

Auf die Frage nach den maßgeblichen Ursachen für die anhaltende Schwächephase benennen die befragten Unternehmen drei zentrale Faktoren:

- Rohstoff- und Energiekosten: 80 Prozent der Firmen, die eine schwache Konjunktur erwarten, sehen in den Energie- und Rohstoffpreisen das größte Hindernis.
- Arbeitskosten und Abgaben: 75 Prozent führen steigende Arbeitskosten einschließlich der Sozialabgaben als wesentlichen Belastungsfaktor an.
- Standortbedingungen: 71 Prozent der Betriebe vermissen konkrete Verbesserungen bei den allgemeinen Rahmenbedingungen in Deutschland.
Die Umfragedaten stützen die wiederholte Kritik an ausbleibenden Reformen , auf die Ökonominnen und Ökonomen regelmäßig hinweisen. Wirtschaftsverbände und Forschungsinstitute mahnen verlässliche Schritte bei Energiekosten und Standortpolitik an, damit aus den theoretischen Wachstumsprognosen ein spürbarer Aufschwung in der Praxis werden kann. Verwendete Quellen: dpa, funkemedien.de, iwkoeln.de (ph)

articleBody:
Eczema causes itchy, inflamed rashes on the skin

Evgeniia Gordeeva/Getty Images

Over a third of people with moderate to severe eczema taking part in a clinical trial have seen their skin completely or almost completely clear up after taking an experimental pill for four months. The drug targets a part of the immune system that causes eczema when it gets stuck in overdrive, and it may be preferable to the current standard treatment, which has to be injected.

“It definitely looks promising,” says [Gayle Ross](https://www.thermh.org.au/our-people/gayle-ross) at the Royal Melbourne Hospital.

[Read more Chronic inflammation messes with your mind. Here’s how to calm it](https://www.newscientist.com/article/2491017-chronic-inflammation-messes-with-your-mind-heres-how-to-calm-it/)

Eczema, or atopic dermatitis, is a chronic skin condition characterised by itchy, inflamed rashes and broken skin that can become infected. It is driven by an overactive immune pathway involving two signalling proteins called interleukin-4 and interleukin-13.

In 2017, the companies Sanofi and Regeneron received approval in the US for their jointly developed eczema drug dupilumab, which blocks interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 signalling. But, although the medication is [effective](https://www.dupixenthcp.com/atopicdermatitis/efficacy-safety/adult-real-world-results), it has had [limited uptake](https://www.sciencedirect.com/org/science/article/pii/S256209592300065X) in the US because it must be injected under the skin and costs up to $59,000 per year for those without insurance coverage.

Now, another company, Kymera Therapeutics, has developed an alternative treatment that can be taken in pill form, called KT-621. It targets the same immune pathway as dupilumab but degrades a protein called STAT6 that is activated downstream from interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 in the development of eczema.

Free newsletter

#### Sign up to Health Check

[Sign up to newsletter](https://www.newscientist.com/sign-up/health/)

In the [clinical trial](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07217015), 244 adults with an average age of 39 and moderate to severe eczema were randomised to take KT-621 at three different doses or a placebo pill every day for 16 weeks.

Those taking the most effective dose experienced an average [72 per cent reduction](https://investors.kymeratx.com/news-releases/news-release-details/kymera-therapeutics-announces-positive-results-broaden2-phase-2b) in their eczema severity on a standard scale, compared to 27 per cent in the placebo group. What’s more, 38 per cent of participants taking KT-621 had completely healed skin or almost completely healed skin by the end of the trial.

“These results exceeded our expectations,” said [Terence Rooney](https://www.kymeratx.com/about-us/leadership/terence-rooney-md/), the chief medical officer of Kymera Therapeutics, when announcing the results in a [webcast](https://investors.kymeratx.com/news-releases/news-release-details/kymera-therapeutics-announces-positive-results-broaden2-phase-2b) on 23 November. He showed before-and-after photos of one man who had had severe eczema all over his torso at the beginning of the trial, which disappeared by the end.

“It’s obviously early days and the trial had relatively small patient numbers, but [KT-621] looks like it has similar efficacy to dupilumab, which is currently the standard of care for moderate to severe atopic dermatitis, and it would be nice to have an oral option as opposed to an injection,” says Ross.

[Read more You can upgrade your immune system, but not in the way you think](https://www.newscientist.com/article/2507511-you-can-upgrade-your-immune-system-but-not-in-the-way-you-think/)

The medication also appeared safe. A small proportion of participants developed conjunctivitis as a side-effect, but it tended to be mild and didn’t cause anyone to discontinue treatment, said Rooney. In fact, since the trial, almost every participant has chosen to continue taking the daily pill as part of an ongoing study, he said.

People taking dupilumab can develop conjunctivitis too, so “we’re pretty used to dealing with that”, says Ross.

Kymera Therapeutics is now planning a larger trial of KT-621 for treating eczema that is scheduled to begin in mid-2027. The company is also currently running a [trial of KT-621 in people with asthma](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07323654), since the condition is caused by the same overactive immune pathway operating in the lungs. It hasn’t yet said how much the drug will cost if it eventually receives regulatory approval.

title: How Important Were Medieval Viking Drinking Games?
subtitle: It’s clear from mythology that alcohol was ritually significant in Norse culture, and none more so than mead, which was considered a godly drink an…

articleBody:
It’s clear from mythology that alcohol was ritually significant in Norse culture, and none more so than mead, which was considered a godly drink and one that imbued the drinker with poetic skill.

In the ancient sagas the origin story of mead comes from a daring series of thefts, with the drink first created through the spit-based peace negotiations of two warring god-families. Their congealing spit, naturally, birthed a mystic with the highest intelligence called Kvasir whose blood was in fact all mead, and through this blood flowed poetry itself.

Unfortunately, Kvasir was not intelligent enough to avoid murder by dwarves for his blood-mead, and then this precious liquid was stolen again by a giant. Odin, king of the gods, wanted his own share of this bloody-mega-mead and so disguised himself as an eagle and stole the mead from the giant, allegedly seducing the giant’s daughter in the process. As Odin escaped from the giant’s lair, some of the mead was spilled from his eagle’s beak and fell to earth. It was said that the great Norse saga poets were those folk who by luck were struck by drops of falling mead from Odin’s beak.

Booze was a bind which helped keep Norse society together, with shared drinking a way of professing loyalty.

Beyond the wild and winding escapades of the gods in pursuit of blood-mead, we know a lot of drinking also happened in the mortal Norse realms. Booze was a bind which helped keep Norse society together, with shared drinking a way of professing loyalty and signing contracts, from marriage to inheritance. This drinking, along with most other gatherings (and anything else, for that matter), would take place in the hall, the only place to be in Norse society, what with the winter weather and limited fuel for fires. It was in these halls that the very important business of feast-throwing and drinking in honor of a lord or warrior would take place.

The feast, a sometimes days- or weeks-long exhibition of power and hospitality by the host, was a common (if extraordinarily expensive) way of gift-giving and demon-strating respect among the elites of Norse society. A big bouquet for your sister’s birthday or a nice dessert to take to your aunt’s weekend lunch seems more reasonable now. Great halls designed for this purpose would ring with music, played on bone flutes, bells, stringed instruments and rattles, as well as shields, which were beaten as drums. Such music would be accompanied by other entertainment, including dramatic performances of the old sagas. Drinking was such an integral part of these feasting celebrations that some later sagas show those who did not drink being ostracized from the retinue of their host with some hostility, their lack of involvement seen as an affront.

This binding together of drinkers was done through a (perhaps unhygienic) custom of *sumbl*, a ritual ceremony also known as “oath cup,” where a woman, often related to the host, would share out a ritual drink among the gathering, one sip at a time and from the same glass. It’s possible women undertook this as a nod to their perceived magical power, and their role as brewers too. The order of those served would help establish the hierarchy of the gathering, a diplomatic tightrope no doubt decided carefully by the hosting household. In the sagas, this drinking ritual was often accompanied by an oath or vow.

In *Beowulf*, an Anglo-Saxon poem recounting a saga, Queen Wealhtheow is the cupbearer at a *sumbl*, greeting her husband and king, Horthgar, with drink first before serving others in turn. Beowulf the warrior takes an oath through this ceremony of the *bragafull* after being challenged by the Queen to rid her hall, the hall of Heorot, of the evil beast that stalks it. Oath-making and -keeping, though, could be lower stakes than defending a hall from its dragon enemies; marriages, alliances and other agreements were kept as oaths, and bound often with communal drinking as a shared witness.

For those not rich, battle-famous or influential enough to be invited to the great feasts in the chieftain’s hall, they too found a way to enjoy a glass or two after a tough day on the fjords. This took place in the *Skytningar*, a more informal refectory, essentially a pub, where individuals paid their own dues, rather than the quite expensive business of throwing a feast and footing the bill for everyone. As a result, these drinking places attracted the less wealthy looking for a fix, like farmers, merchants and townsfolk. These everyday dives tended to have a pretty bad reputation, the mark of a good time no doubt.

Foreign merchants were often blamed for the noisy impact of these drinking houses on their surroundings, with Snorri’s *Olaf’s saga* recording how between 1067 and 1093 King Óláfr Haraldsson Kyrri was displeased with the “drinking bouts in marketplaces about the land as a consequence of the large number of merchants.” Later Norwegian kings also continued to rail against the drunkenness of the common man, with King Sverrir in 1300 making a speech against the drunkenness of both his people and the troublesome Germans, who had proved such effective merchants that the stronger wine they traded could now be bought at a price equivalent to local ales, causing outrageous drunkenness among townsfolk.

From gods stealing blood-mead from their giant enemies, to warrior chieftains feasting, toasting and oath making in their great halls, Norse society was intertwined with alcohol.

From gods stealing blood-mead from their giant enemies, to warrior chieftains feasting, toasting and oath making in their great halls, Norse society was intertwined with alcohol, often with a rich societal meaning. Yet this seriousness wasn’t the only way drinking was done; in fact, a range of less formal and honourable drinking methods exist in the form of Norse drinking games.

Many sagas tell of drinking competitions, including those taking place between guests at feasts in the game of *mannjafnaor*. The game was essentially a bragging match in which men and sometimes women pitted their wits against each other to rank themselves against the rest. Often tasked with debating who was the greater warrior, based on their athleticism or attractiveness or their preeminence in a given district or hall, debates were quarrelsome and raucous. Such preening could quickly turn sour and descend into another drinking game called *senna,* a form of one-on-one competitive insulting before a crowd, often done in exaggerated poetic verse, with horns of ale drunk between verses which turned this rap battle into a drinking match, as the wit of insult and the strength of stomach were tested before the halls. In one example from a saga, three men exchange round after round of *senna*, drinking horns of ale between each battle:

The king’s men listen to the entertainment. And they took Oddr the horns and he quaffed them both. After that Oddr rises up and goes towards them and he realises that they are conquered by the drink and at the same time that they were beyond composing poetry.

Hnùtukast was another drinking game and one probably left to the very end of the evening as it required none of the brazen boasting or eye-watering insults of Mannjafnaor or Senna. In this simple game, guests would take the bones left over from the meal and, agreeing a series of targets that didn’t necessarily exclude living ones, take it in turns to launch them, with the least successful no doubt receiving a forfeit, perhaps of drinking yet more again.

Other silly feast- (and we can therefore read drink-) related games litter the sagas left to us by the Norse Skald poets, from swimming competitions and testing duels to competitions where challengers would see who could hold their head longest under water in a barrel. Evidently almost anything in a hall full of ale-addled men could become a drinking game.

______________________________

*From* [History’s Greatest Drinking Games: From the Notorious to the Wisely Forgotten](https://bookshop.org/a/132/9781250453785) *by Elliot Martyn. Copyright © 2026 by Elliot Martyn. Available from St. Martin’s Press, an imprint of St. Martin’s Publishing Group.*

A study of the largest available Chinese lifespan-wide structural neuroimaging dataset (comprising 43,037 participants aged 0–100 years) established population-specific brain charts, revealing developmental trajectories that diverge from those of predominantly white populations. These tailored charts improved typical phenotypic prediction and better captured disease-related deviations, advancing equitable precision neuroscience.

articleBody:
As [MusicTech wrote](https://musictech.com/reviews/plug-ins/baby-audio-transit-2-review-andrew-huang/) when Baby Audio’s Transit 2 multi-effects unit came out in 2024, “this plugin is actually awesome.” Now producers can get this top tier addition to their arsenal for the insanely low price of £49. That’s 50% off the original price of £99.

[deals ids=”3487195c-50c6-4e4d-a063-25acd15047ae”]

But what’s in the box (pun intended) when you buy this revered product? To start there are 28 effects modules that can be operated with six different motion modes. Its bread and butter is its huge capability for creating interesting transitions between different moments in a song. Instead of obsessing over automation, use one single knob on the Transit 2 to add effects sweeps spanning everything from digital chorus to tremolo to noise to flanger.

Moreover, there over 400 presets from primary designer Andrew Huang to use for yourself or to act as a foundation for your own exploration. Another approach is Transit 2’s randomisation engine. Create something completely new with the click of a button or define the process with different random ranges to affect certain parameters with the function.

Transit 1 only had 18 effects. With 10 new ones, there is simply no limits to the combinations of effects users can create and how those can interact with the music. Other than that there are four new motion modes to control how the knob will action the effects chains. To maximise how the motion and the effects work together, every element of each effect and can be added or removed from the motion parameters as well.

articleBody:
**Geburtstag, Jahrestag, Weihnachten, Namenstag… Das Jahr steckt voller Gelegenheiten, ein geliebtes Gesicht zum strahlen zu bringen! Dein bester Kumpel macht sich als Musikproduzent selbständig und hofft auf deine Unterstützung? Die Lebensgefährtin träumt vom eigenen, professionell produzierten Podcast? Keinen Bock mehr auf Omas Häkeldecken-Pakete zu jedem Anlass? Diese Producer-Geschenktipps verschönern jeden Wunschzettel!**

Inhalte

- Warm Audio WA-47jr SE
- Tegeler Audio Crème
- Wavebone Headquarter Wood Studio Desk
- Warm Audio Bus-Comp
- Wavebone Viking Foam Chair
- Warm Audio WA-87jr (SE)
- Warm Audio Jude-MP2

## Warm Audio WA-47jr SE

„Warm und charaktervoll“, so [klingt das WA-47jr SE](https://www.bonedo.de/artikel/warm-audio-wa-47jr-se-test/)! Wenige Zahlen machen Musikproduzenten den Mund so wässrig wie die 47, denn sie verweist in der Audiotechnik auf das legendäre Neumann U47. Das [WA-47jr ‘Studio Essentials’](https://www.thomann.de/de/warm_audio_wa_47jr_se.htm?offid=1&affid=84)bringt dir einen ähnlichen Vintage-Sound wie das vergriffene Original zu einem Bruchteil des Preises. Das Studiomikro ist schnörkellos auf’s Wesentliche reduziert: Es hat die wohl am meisten genutzte Richtcharakteristik (Niere), kommt ohne Röhren und Übertrager aus und verzichtet auf Extras wie Pad, Filter und Spinne. Dafür bekommst du für kleine Maus ein charaktervolles Werkzeug für deine Gesangs- und Instrumental-Produktionen oder die deiner Liebsten! Zwei Finishes stehen zur Auswahl.

## Tegeler Audio Crème

Was nützt das beste Signal ohne die passende Bearbeitung? [Tegeler Audios Stereo-Prozessor Crème](https://www.thomann.de/de/tegeler_creme_green.htm?offid=1&affid=84) sitzt perfekt auf der Summe, veredelt aber schon beim Recording deine Einzelspuren: Der VCA-Kompressor mit Sidechain-Filter beherrscht sanfte Verdichtung ebenso wie Punch und Limiting, die Chicken Head-Potis und das VU-Meter versprühen Vintage-Charm in der Bedienung und die [Filterbänder der EQ-Sektion im Pultec-Stil arbeiten äußerst musikalisch](https://www.bonedo.de/artikel/tegeler-audio-manufaktur-creme-test/)! Klar, zweikanalig und Made in Germany hat das seinen Preis. Vielleicht sagst du den Arbeitskollegen, sie sollen bei deinem Dienstaustritt auf die goldene Uhr zugunsten des Crème verzichten?

## Wavebone Headquarter Wood Studio Desk

Schwebendes Streicherarrangement in deinem Popsong? Klavier-Intro und Rhodes-Sound für die Power-Ballade? Ja gerne, am einfachsten als virtuelle Instrumente. Nur, wohin mit dem 88-tastigen Masterkeyboard? Die elegante Lösung: [Wavebones Headquarter Wood Studio Desk](https://www.thomann.de/de/wavebone_headquarter_wood.htm?offid=1&affid=84) mit höhenverstellbarer Keyboardablage auf Rollen! Für die Keys hast du sechs Positionen zur Auswahl, der stabile Tisch aus Stahl und MDF bietet eine erhöhte Ablage für deine Monitore und eine optionale Kabelhalterung gibt’s auch. Tipp: Schenk dir den Wavebone einfach selbst, ohne, dass es jemand merkt. „Scha-haaatz, wolltest du nicht schon lange einen neuen Wohnzimmertisch? Ich hab da ein total stylishes Modell in Walnussholz-Optik gefunden…“

## Warm Audio Bus-Comp

u träumst vom perfekten Mix-Glue, deine Oma sagt aber, mehr als 800 Euro gibt’s dieses Jahr nicht zu Weihnachten? Dann kannst du den [SSL Bus-Kompressor](https://www.bonedo.de/artikel/ssl-bus-comp-classic-test/) wohl vergessen, seinen Sound aber nicht! Denn der [zweikanalige Warm Audio Bus-Comp](https://www.thomann.de/de/warm_audio_bus_comp.htm?offid=1&affid=84) macht seine Sache außerordentlich gut und bietet gegenüber dem Original sogar eine [„erweiterte Threshold-Range“ und einen „höher angesetzten Gain-Umfang“](https://www.bonedo.de/artikel/warm-audio-bus-comp-test/). Die Cinemag-Transformer im Signalweg sind schaltbar und die Rückseite bietet zusätzlich zu den XLRs Klinken-Ins und Outs. Frohes Fest!

Studiostandards: Kompressoren und Limiter

Manche Kompressoren, wie den LA-3A, den 1176 oder einen API 2500 findet man in der Mehrzahl der Studios – oder Varianten davon. Wieso bloß?

12.01.2016

4,5 / 5

2

Zum Test

## Wavebone Viking Foam Chair

Mal eben vom Mischpult wegdrehen, die Klampfe greifen und die Idee festhalten, die im Kopf rumschwirrt: Mit dem Wavebone Viking Foam Chair kinderleicht! Denn der ergonomische Stuhl ist auf das schnelle Navigieren im Studio zwischen Spielen, Mischen und Editieren abgestimmt. Seine Armlehnen klappst du weg, er gleitet auf leisen, Parkett-schonenden PU-Rollen und du stellst den Wikinger mit wenigen Handgriffen optimal auf deine Rückenlänge und Sitzposition ein. Doch das Beste kommt noch: Mama und Papa werden glauben, ihr Kind sei endlich vernünftig und mache doch noch etwas Anständiges aus seinem Leben, weil du dir zum Geburtstag einen ergonomischen ‘Bürostuhl’ wünschst!

## Warm Audio WA-87jr (SE)

Die 87 ist noch so eine magische Zahl unter Audioingenieuren, denn das Neumann U87 ist aufgrund seiner Allrounder-Qualitäten ein Desert Island Mic. Wenn du die Million Euro noch nicht geknackt hast, verschenkst du zum Fest besser erst einmal ein dem Original nachempfundenes [Warm Audio WA-87](https://www.bonedo.de/artikel/warm-audio-wa87-test/), das es in verschiedenen klanglich überzeugenden Varianten gibt. ‘Junior’ ist die übertragerlose FET-Version. Dank Doppelmembrankapsel schaltest du die Richtcharakteristik (Niere, Acht, Kugel) wie beim WA-87 und bekommt eine Spinne und ein Ledertäschchen als Zubehör. Das [Warm Audio WA-87jr](https://www.thomann.de/de/warm_audio_wa_87jr.htm?offid=1&affid=84) kommt in silber und schwarz. Gesang, Sprache, Drum-Overhead, Mikrofonierung der akustischen Gitarre, das WA-87jr macht an vielen Schallquellen eine gute Figur. Die SE-Version hat die feste Richtcharakteristik Niere, dafür legst du auf dem Weg zur ersten Million mehr bei Seite.

Studiostandards: Vocal-Mikrofone

Oh ja, es gibt sie, die klassischen Mikrofone, die für Gesangsaufnahmen in Tonstudios gerne benutzt werden. Und, oh ja: Sie sind teuer bis unbezahlbar. Wir zeigen hier die Klassiker – und preiswerte Alternativen.

articleBody:
## Improving on a timeless recipe

The bezier curve is a staple of CAD and computer graphics. Like Bic pens, the design is decades old and they're everywhere. You'll often find them as the default or only choice in various illustration and animation tools.

Conceived by [Paul de Casteljau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_de_Casteljau) in 1959, and refined by [Pierre Bézier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Bézier) in the 1960s at Renault, the enduring appeal of the bezier curve lies in its simplicity. While more sophisticated curves have been invented, and [new ones continue to be proposed](https://linebender.org/blog/hyperbezier/), these are limited to specific domains, like high-precision CAD or road design. In general use, the bezier stubbornly refuses to be dethroned, despite its shortcomings.

Hence bezier curves are a piece of legacy tech we appear to be stuck with. As a software engineer, my question then is: can we make beziers better without invalidating all the tech built on and with them?

The answer is yes.

[↗ wallup.net](https://wallup.net/renault-4cv-classic-cars-french-73/)

## Lerp-a-derp

Drawing a bezier curve is a surprisingly simple and linear process:

*Tip: All the diagrams in this post are fully interactive.*

Given a series of control points, we connect them with lines. We then run along those lines simultaneously, to produce new points, which can be connected again. This process is repeated until we are left with a single point, which lies on the curve.

This construction makes beziers far more regular than they might first appear.

The linear interpolations (aka *lerps* ) can be summarized into a single compact formula, e.g. for 4 control points $ \left(A, B, C, D\right) $:

$$ \gamma \left( t \right) = A \cdot \left(1 - t\right)^3 + B \cdot 3 \left(1 - t\right)^2 t + C \cdot 3 \left(1 - t\right) t^2 + D \cdot t^3 $$

The rule is simple: descending powers of $\left(1 - t\right)$, ascending powers of $t$, with coefficients taken from the n'th row of Pascal's triangle:

$$
\ {ccccccccccccc}
&&&&&& 1 \\
&&&&& 1 && 1 \\
&&&& 1 && 2 && 1 \\
&&& 1 && 3 && 3 && 1 \\
&& 1 && 4 && 6 && 4 && 1 \\
&1 && 5 && 10 && 10 && 5 && 1 \\
... &&&&&&... &&&&&&... \\
\ $$

For curves in 2D and 3D, the formula is applied to the individual X, Y or Z coordinates.

While beziers can be constructed for any number of control points, the common practice is to only use cubic beziers with 4 control points. This is because the curve is only guaranteed to cross through the first and last control point, which makes higher degree beziers more difficult to shape.

Larger curves are instead constructed by joining together multiple cubic bezier segments, with the tangents lined up to create a segmented curve that appears smooth:

This is the cubic bezier *spline*, as commonly understood. The precision "pen tool" in most drawing apps then consists of drawing and editing the control points, rather than drawing curves directly.

## A Lie Told Everywhere

Pen tools typically have a few different modes for the control points:

Intuitively these represent various degrees of smoothness. Symmetric tangents are offered as the smoothest option, with some qualities of smoothness being lost as you relax the constraints.

In reality this is **completely wrong**, and this is easy to demonstrate.

Bezier curves can be split exactly, by reading off the new control points from the interpolation diagram:

The left and right segments are 100% identical to the original curve, and always join up perfectly at the seam. Yet the tangents in the middle will be asymmetric except for one split near the middle. This can be confirmed using a *curvature comb* which represents the (inverse) radius of curvature at every point:

The curvature comb remains continuous, with no jumps.

This means that whether or not adjacent tangents are of equal length, i.e. symmetric, is completely irrelevant. Attempting to draw smooth and intuitive bezier curves this way is a fool's errand.

A simple way to improve this is to treat the tangents as relative rather than absolute. e.g. We can make them proportional to the distance between the start and end of each segment:

This spline is easier to edit, because as you move each curve point around, the adjacent segments naturally flex to get out of the way. There are far fewer cusps created this way. Editing the tangents remains the same.

However if we plot curvature again, we can tell this isn't a great solution:

Scaling tangents proportionally doesn't guarantee that curvature is preserved as you edit, nor does curvature remain continuous from one segment to the next.

This also shows that offering users a curvature comb visualization as a "helpful tool" is really quite *mean*: adjusting the curvature on one end will also affect the other side, requiring repeated adjustments back and forth until it's close enough.

## Handle Carefully

A much more effective strategy is to work with curvature directly.

While this is a difficult problem in general, it turns out there are some surprising relationships here, which we can observe directly:

Consider the curvature at the start of segment $A-B-C-D$. This is affected only by the positions of $A$, $B$ and $C$. Point $D$ can be moved freely if it's detached from $C$.

Furthermore, because the tangent $A-B$ is horizontal, only the vertical position of $C$ matters. This is a result of the underlying linear interpolations, which end up cancelling out a lot of terms in the formulas.

The curvature at $A$ is therefor only affected by the length of $A-B$, and the perpendicular distance from $C$ to $A-B$. The same applies to $D$ on the other side with $C-D$ and $B$.

This isn't very useful by itself though. When we move a curve point ($A$ or $D$), typically the adjacent control point ($B$ or $C$) is moved as well to preserve the tangent. And when we turn a symmetric or asymmetric tangent, the adjacent tangent in the next segment is turned by the same angle, altering the curvature on that side.

Still, this shows that preserving curvature is not by itself a crazy idea and can be done simply by scaling the tangents appropriately. The rules would be simple:

- When we move a curve point, we have to preserve the start and end curvature in the adjacent segments
- When we move a tangent, we have to preserve the curvature on the opposite end of the current segment, as well as on both sides of the adjacent segment

This ought to produce an editing experience where the curve actually respects your intent. Except not quite:

Moving curve points works great, but when turning a tangent, the length of that tangent is itself a poor representation of the user's intent. Small changes can cause huge shifts in curvature, which can cause the curve to jump around and explode unexpectedly as it tries to find a matching solution.

Hence it's better to work with curvature handles instead, where the length corresponds directly to curvature:

Unlike the curvature comb, the length of the handles is the non-inverted radius of curvature, which is the more natural choice.

These handles are very stable and can be converted just-in-time to classic bezier control points, without needing to round-trip back and forth between the two representations. Helpfully, this also avoids numerical drift.

## Goldilocks

To actually pull this off, we need to solve for the lengths $l_0$ and $l_1$ of the tangents, given the desired curvatures $k_0$ and $k_1$, the start/end points $A$ and $D$, and the unit-length tangents at the start/end.

Given a curve $\gamma\left(t\right)$, we can express the unit tangent vector $\ \left(t\right)$ as the normalized derivative:

$$ \ \left(t\right) = \ {\displaystyle |γ'\left(t\right)|} $$

This can be used to find the curvature vector $\ \left(t\right)$ via two vector cross products using the first and second derivative:

$$ \ \left(t\right) = \ \left(t\right) \times \ {|\gamma'\left(t\right)|^2} \times \ \left(t\right) $$

The cross products ensure that $\ \left(t\right)$ is perpendicular to $\ \left(t\right)$, i.e. they extract the normal vector component of the middle term. Now we can solve for $\ \left(0\right) = k_0$ and $\ \left(1\right) = k_1$.

After working through the math, we end up with a quadratic system of equations in $l_0$ and $l_1$:

$$
\ a_0 \cdot l_0^2 + b \cdot l_1 + c_0 = 0 \\[0.3em]
a_1 \cdot l_1^2 + b \cdot l_0 + c_1 = 0
\ $$

Where:

$$
\ {lcl}
a_0 & = & ±|k_0| \\[0.3em]
a_1 & = & ±|k_1| \\[0.3em]
b & = & 2 \cdot |\ (0) \times \ (1)| \\[0.3em]
c_0 & = & 6 \cdot |\ (0) \times (D - A)| \\[0.3em]
c_1 & = & 6 \cdot |\ (1) \times (A - D)| \\[0.3em]
\ $$

This captures a few things:

- The sign of the curvature $k_i$ defines whether the curve turns clockwise or counterclockwise. When moving curve points around, the curve may be forced to flip, hence the $±$ is necessary, and both signs can change independently.
- The coupling between $l_0$ and $l_1$ is influenced only by $b$. If $b = 0$, then the two equations are independent and the problem is trivial to solve. This corresponds to the situation where the two tangents are parallel.
- The constant term $c_i$ is influenced only by the perpendicular distance $D - A$ (or $A - D$) to the tangent $\ $. This matches the earlier finding that only perpendicular distance affects curvature.

Hence, the problem is reduced to finding the intersection of two double-parabolas, one horizontal and one vertical:

The two sides of each double-parabola represent bending clockwise or counterclockwise. We have to solve 4 times, one for each sign combination $\left(+,+\right)$, $\left(+,-\right)$, $\left(-,+\right)$, $\left(-,-\right)$.

To solve this system, we can rewrite either of the equations to isolate $l_1$ or $l_0$:

$$
l_1 = \ {\displaystyle b} \\[0.5em]
l_0 = \ {\displaystyle b}
$$

Pick one, and square it to plug it into the other original equation as the $l_1^2$ or $l_0^2$ term. This produces a quartic equation in the other variable (resp. $l_0$ or $l_1$), which can be solved directly using the quartic formula.

We can then compute the other $l_i$, either:

$$
l_1 = \ {\displaystyle a_1}} \\[0.5em]
l_0 = \ {\displaystyle a_0}}
$$

Not all solutions of the quartic will be actual solutions to the system however, because of the squaring. So we have to double check that the original equations hold before accepting a solution for $\left(l_0, l_1\right)$.

We also want to reject solutions where $l_0 < 0$ or $l_1 < 0$, because these represent situations where the tangents have been flipped by 180º.

In most cases, there will only be one valid solution, and this works pretty well:

For corner-type points, one or both $k_i$'s are infinite. This is straightforward to solve as the matching $l_i$ is zero and the other can be computed directly.

## Grouper and Snapper

Unfortunately if there are multiple solutions, these each represent a different curve:

Having the curve jump around as you edit it would be a very bad editing experience, but there is no obvious way to pick the right one.

One strategy would be to remember the previous $l_0$ and $l_1$ as you edit, and pick the solution that is closest to the previous curve. However this would introduce path-dependence into editing, where the order and direction that you moved points around in affects which curve you end up with. For a drawing tool, this is quite frustrating and undesirable.

Different solutions to the equation can also appear and vanish suddenly, so this wouldn't eliminate popping either, merely reduce it.

Ideally the resulting curvatures should always change smoothly themselves. This can be accomplished by designing an appropriate weighting heuristic for the solutions, and calculating their weighted average.

1) The forbidden regions:

When a solution approaches either $l_0 < 0$ or $l_1 < 0$, it's about to vanish, so its weight should go to zero there.

2) When two opposite-bending parabolas are about to become tangent, two solutions will move towards each other, before both vanishing at the same time:

These solutions are unstable and should be avoided. To detect this, I calculate the gradient vector of each equation.

$$
\ = \ 2 \cdot a_0 \cdot l_0 & b\ \\[0.3em]
\ = \ b & 2 \cdot a_1 \cdot l_1\ $$

The angle between them can be found via their dot product, after dividing by their respective lengths:

$$
\cos \theta = \ \cdot \ }{\displaystyle |\ ||\ |}
$$

A value close to $-1$ means two opposite-bending parabolas, while a value close to $1$ means two aligned parabolas. The latter is not as bad, as this implies many almost-equivalent solutions.

3) When the radius of curvature is very big compared to the bezier itself, one of the possible solutions is for the curve to cross through itself, forming a loop. This should be discouraged:

We can divide by the length of $|\ |$ i.e. $\ $, preferring solutions that have shorter tangents.

Putting it all together, the weighting heuristic I chose is:

$$
\left(\ \right) = \left(\ {\displaystyle |\ |^2}\right)^2
$$

- By applying $\arccos \left(-\cos \theta\right)$, we remap the dot-product range $(-1..1)$ to $(0..π)$ which effectively neutralizes the unstable solutions
- Large $|\ |$'s represent undesirable solutions, so should be strongly penalized and only chosen if they are the only option
- When the entire heuristic approaches $0$, the influence should vanish smoothly, hence the overall squaring

Using this as the weight, the resulting bezier curves always change smoothly, even when the start and end are moved around and through each other.

But when multiple solutions are averaged together, the resulting $(l_0, l_1)$ is not necessarily a solution to the original system. This means the resulting curvatures are not always exact, even when there is an exact solution nearby.

To mitigate this, we can add an additional resampling step, where we re-weigh the solutions according to the inverse distance^4 to the weighted average:

$$
\left(\ \right) = \ {|\ - \ |^4}
$$

This causes the solution to snap smoothly to exact solutions when available.

## Migratory Curves

What's especially nice about this approach is that it can largely be slotted into existing systems with little modification required.

The UI of adjusting and editing bezier handles can be kept, including the notion of the 4 point types. Just the meaning of the lengths of the tangents changes. Converting an asymmetric point to a symmetric point will actually equalize the curvature of the left and right side, which is what the user actually wants.

The internal representation can mostly remain the same type, i.e. a series of points, just those points represent curvature tangents, not bezier tangents. Though it's better to explicitly store the unit length tangents and curvatures directly, which is more numerically stable. For the demos here I made pairwise conversion functions between curvature handles ↔︎ points/tangents/curvatures ↔︎ bezier handles.

Splitting a curvature bezier is a lot simpler than splitting a classic bezier, because the start and end handles don't change at all, and the newly created handles are symmetric:

There is one remaining flaw though. When splitting a curve with an S-bend, the splits near the bend are not exact:

The heuristic picks the wrong curve on one or both sides. This can be fixed by remembering the specific orientation of the curvature, and only flipping the curvature sign when necessary. Though this does introduce some minimal path-dependence into editing.

So really you would need to expose this in the UI as an extra orientation toggle for ambiguous control points. It would also mean that the internal representation has to be in tangent + signed curvature form to be fully stable, not just curvature handles.

Near the S-bend, the radius of curvature—and thus the handle size—effectively becomes infinite, because $|k|$ becomes $0$. The bezier control points lie on a straight line, as perpendicular distance to the tangent is zero.

So even when handled exactly, this can still create impractically large curvature handles. Perhaps what's needed is a 5th "Inflection" point type, for points with exactly zero $|k|$, though such points tend to be very unstable, and sometimes no solution exists:

To migrate a classic bezier to a curvature bezier, you can measure the unit tangents and curvature at the start and end. In the vast majority of cases this will result in the exact same curve. If it doesn't, then you must split the original bezier to avoid the ambiguity.

For complex operations on bezier curves, e.g. boolean union or intersection, these still have to be done in bezier form. This implies some amount of round-tripping between the two representations, which would introduce numerical drift. However, only the newly created points need to be converted back, because the curvature and tangents elsewhere remain the same.

* * *

This post started from the observation that "symmetric" bezier tangents aren't actually symmetric as you'd expect. Hopefully you found the resulting exploration enlightening.

The practice of showing curvature combs to diagnose problems with splines is really backwards. If we can show a curvature comb, we can also compute an appropriate spline to match the desired curvature.

So beziers as they commonly exist are quite inadequate. We can retrofit a better system to edit them without breaking the expectations of a smooth editing experience, or introducing a new class of curves that behaves very differently.

*The code for the diagrams and implementation can be found on [GitLab](https://gitlab.com/unconed/bezbox/-/blob/master/src/graph/bez.ts?ref_type=heads#L61).*

articleBody:
DRESDEN. **Auch wenn sie zunächst wie ein Makel im Zeugnis erscheinen: Schlechte Kopfnoten können Schülerinnen und Schüler noch Jahrzehnte später weiterbringen. Denn Hinweise auf mangelnde Konzentration, Unruhe oder Schwierigkeiten im Sozialverhalten können helfen, psychische Auffälligkeiten zu erkennen und richtig einzuordnen. Wie wertvoll solche Beobachtungen sind, zeigen neue wissenschaftliche Erkenntnisse zur Diagnostik von ADHS. Ein Kinder- und Jugendpsychiater warnt deshalb davor, die schriftlichen Beurteilungen von Lehrkräften abzuschaffen. Anlass ist eine geplante Reform in Sachsen.**

ADHS? (Symbolbild.) Illustration: News4teachers

Was Lehrkräfte über das Arbeits- und Sozialverhalten ihrer Schülerinnen und Schüler festhalten, kann noch Jahrzehnte später von Bedeutung sein. Gerade bei der Diagnose psychischer Erkrankungen wie ADHS oder Autismus liefern alte Schulzeugnisse wichtige Hinweise darauf, wie sich Auffälligkeiten bereits in der Kindheit gezeigt haben. Der Dresdner Kinder- und Jugendpsychiater Veit Roessner warnt deshalb davor, schriftliche Beurteilungen abzuschaffen. «Die Psychiatrie braucht die Informationen aus den Kopfnoten. Was Lehrkräfte über ein Kind festhalten, hilft uns oft bei der Diagnostik», sagt der Direktor der Kinder- und Jugendpsychiatrie am Universitätsklinikum Dresden. Anlass seiner Warnung ist eine geplante Reform in Sachsen, bei der die bislang verpflichtenden schriftlichen Einschätzungen künftig freiwillig werden könnten.

Sachsen will die bisherigen Noten für Betragen, Fleiß, Mitarbeit und Ordnung überarbeiten. Eine Kommission soll bis Jahresende Vorschläge vorlegen, welche Kompetenzen künftig benotet werden. Mit Blick auf die Arbeitsbelastung von Lehrkräften soll es ihnen selbst überlassen bleiben, ob sie eine zusätzliche schriftliche Einschätzung der Schülerinnen und Schüler auf dem Jahreszeugnis formulieren.

## Alte Zeugnisse helfen beim Blick auf die Kindheit enorm

Die kinder- und jugendpsychiatrische Diagnostik nutze Schulzeugnisse regelmäßig, sagt Roessner. Bei vielen psychischen Erkrankungen sei es wichtig, die Entwicklung von Verhalten und Fähigkeiten nachzuvollziehen. «Lehrkräfte verfügen durch ihre Erfahrung mit Tausenden Kindern und Jugendlichen über besondere Fähigkeiten, Verhalten altersgerecht einzuordnen. Ihre regelmäßigen schriftlichen Beurteilungen dokumentieren zeitnah, wie sich ein Kind entwickelt hat. Damit ergänzen sie die oft lückenhaften oder im Rückblick verzerrten Erinnerungen der Betroffenen und ihrer Eltern.»

«Die Diagnostik psychischer Erkrankungen wie ADHS oder Autismus benötigt Informationen darüber, wie sich Auffälligkeiten im Laufe der Kindheit und Jugend entwickelt haben», betonte der Professor. «Gerade bei einer erstmaligen ADHS-Diagnose im Erwachsenenalter müssen wir oft Jahrzehnte zurückblicken. Erinnerungen der Betroffenen und ihrer Eltern sind häufig ungenau oder verzerrt. Schulzeugnisse dokumentieren dagegen die damaligen Beobachtungen von Lehrkräften, die auch Jahrzehnte später noch unverändert vorliegen.»

Ein Forschungsteam mit Beteiligung Roessners untersuchte erstmals den diagnostischen Nutzen der schriftlichen Beurteilungen in mehr als 1.800 Grundschulzeugnissen. Die 2025 veröffentlichte Studie zeigte, dass sich anhand der Verhaltensbeschreibungen in den Kopfnoten Kinder mit und ohne ADHS (Aufmerksamkeitsdefizit/Hyperaktivitätsstörung) mit hoher diagnostischer Genauigkeit unterscheiden ließen. Daraus entwickelten die Wissenschaftler das 2026 veröffentlichte Auswertungsverfahren ADHS-ZEBRA.

## Schulische Beurteilungen sind bei Diagnosen von großem Wert

«Für die Kinder- und Jugendpsychiatrie, aber auch für die Erwachsenenpsychiatrie, sind die schulischen Beurteilungen von erheblichem Wert bei etlichen Diagnosen», argumentierte Roessner. Eine Diagnose allein anhand von Zeugnissen zu stellen, sei allerdings nicht möglich. Die Informationen müssten mit weiteren klinischen Befunden zusammengeführt werden. Nicht die einzelnen Schul- oder Kopfnoten seien diagnostisch besonders wertvoll, sondern die konkreten Beobachtungen der Lehrkräfte zur Entwicklung, zu den Fähigkeiten und zum Verhalten eines Kindes.

Wenn Sachsen nun im Zuge einer Reform gerade auf die ergänzenden, ausformulierten Beurteilungen der Lehrkräfte verzichten sollte, könnte damit eine für die medizinische Diagnostik wichtige Informationsquelle verloren gehen, betonte Roessner. «Dabei geht es keineswegs darum, Kinder wegen krankheitsbedingter Verhaltensauffälligkeiten mit schlechten Noten zu bestrafen. Vielmehr sollten diese wichtigen Beobachtungen möglichst sachlich, differenziert und frei von Stigmatisierung dokumentiert werden.»

## Experte plädiert für Erhalt schriftlicher Einschätzungen

Roessner plädiert deshalb dafür, aussagekräftige möglichst umfangreiche Einschätzungen zur Entwicklung, zu den Fähigkeiten und zum Verhalten der Kinder auch künftig zu erhalten. «Für uns ist entscheidend, dass konkrete Beobachtungen zu Stärken und Schwierigkeiten eines Kindes schriftlich festgehalten werden. Über Bezeichnung, Kategorien und Form der Kopfnoten lässt sich selbstverständlich diskutieren.»

Der Ruf nach Entlastung der Lehrkräfte sei berechtigt. Allerdings dürften die Folgen für die psychiatrische Diagnostik nicht übersehen werden. «Was nicht schriftlich durch die Experten Lehrer beurteilt und festgehalten wurde, können wir nicht mehr nachholen», erklärte der Professor.

Die bislang verpflichtende schriftliche Beurteilung ist im sächsischen Schulgesetz geregelt. Über einen Verzicht müsste zunächst der Landtag befinden. Die Gewerkschaft Erziehung und Wissenschaft hatte wiederholt darauf gedrängt.

Sachsens Kultusminister Conrad Clemens (CDU) hält persönlich Kopfnoten für wichtiger denn je. Er kann sich aber vorstellen, die bisherigen Bewertungskategorien neu zu definieren und zu vereinfachen, etwa als Arbeits- und Sozialverhalten. Auch Teamfähigkeit, Respekt oder kreatives Denken könnten eine Rolle spielen. *News4teachers / mit Material der dpa*

title: Seven Books That Show What Architecture Tells Us About Storytelling
subtitle: It was 1976, and as I drove through Marin County, north of San Francisco, an enormous building emerged from the distant hills.

articleBody:
It was 1976, and as I drove through Marin County, north of San Francisco, an enormous building emerged from the distant hills. It seemed almost otherworldly, as if a spacecraft had landed in a field and burrowed its way into the ground.

It was the Marin County Civic Center, designed by Frank Lloyd Wright.

I was captivated by this strange, futuristic building. Its muted pink structure and long, low profile extended into the valley, while its circular and semicircular openings were classical and serene. The building seemed to belong to the landscape even as it challenged it.

I didn’t have the vocabulary then to explain what I was experiencing. I only knew that a structure had altered my perception of the world around it.

Years later, I understood that my draw towards architecture was the relationship between structure and experience. How does a room hold memory? How does a building establish a sense of place? What happens to a structure when people inhabit it, when their histories become entangled with its own?

These questions are not so different from those a writer might ask. A novel, like a building, has a framework (beginning, middle, and end) that holds its parts together: passages that lead us from one place to another, openings that illuminate or obscure a path. Within this framework, writers use language and syntax as an architect uses a straight-edge and pencil. But the most compelling buildings, like the most compelling stories, are more than the sum of their parts. Something happens when human experience enters the structure of both: they’re altered by memory and imagination, capable of holding meanings its creator may never have intended.

When I write, I return to a handful of books that have helped me think about the connections between writing and architecture. Each offers a way of thinking about the relationship between the structures we create and the lives we live within them. And each, in its own way, has something to tell us about storytelling.

**Gaston Bachelard, [The Poetics of Space](https://bookshop.org/a/132/9780143107521)**

A paperback copy of this book was given to me in 1975 by an architect friend. I read it cover to cover and still have that same dog-eared copy, its spine broken, its loose pages held together with tape.

It opened a door for me.

Bachelard writes about the house as a place of reverie and memory. The attic, cellar, drawer, corner, nest—these ordinary spaces become charged with our inner lives. The house is not simply a structure that protects us; it becomes a structure within us.

For writers, Bachelard offers something essential: the understanding that place is never merely a physical backdrop. Rooms can carry emotional history that a character cannot always articulate. The smallest physical detail can be a portal into memory. And often a place we have left behind continues to inhabit us more powerfully than the place in which we presently live.

Bachelard gave me permission to think about architecture lyrically, just as one may think about a poem or prose: the words and the images free our minds up to fall beneath the surface, to tune into the cadence of the subconscious.

**Charles Moore, Gerald Allen, and Donlyn Lyndon, [The Place of Houses](https://bookshop.org/a/132/9780520223578)**

The premise of *The Place of Houses* is deceptively simple: to look closely at the ordinary things that make a house feel uniquely one’s own, while understanding the house within the larger context of its community and landscape. A house should not simply look good from the outside. It should feel good to inhabit.

Something similar happens in fiction. A writer imagines not only the world in which a story takes place, but how a character moves through that world. Where does she feel safe, protected, exposed? What does she see from her window? Which room does she avoid? What does she carry from one place to another?

The relationship between inside and outside is especially compelling. A threshold is never simply a doorway. It marks a passage between different kinds of experience, between the intimacy of the private world and the uncertainty of what lies beyond it.

One of the authors, Donlyn Lyndon, once spoke to me about the importance of establishing a sense of place, of allowing the landscape to suggest the patterns from which the building emerges. I remember the conversation about the wild, unprotected outdoors and the shelter of the interior. Neither could be fully understood without the other; in that understanding, he said, lies the balance between outdoors and indoors.

A story, too, establishes its own geography, of both exposure and refuge. The places characters inhabit can reveal the tensions between their inner and outer lives, often more eloquently than anything they say.

**Christopher Alexander,[A Pattern Language](https://bookshop.org/a/132/9780195019193)**

Christopher Alexander’s *A Pattern Language* proposes that the places in which we feel most comfortable and alive share recurring patterns. These patterns exist at every scale, from the arrangement of a town to the placement of a window seat. They’re not matters of style or taste: they reflect something elemental about the ways human beings seek comfort, connection, privacy, and belonging. Like spoken and written language, which is made up of simple and complex sentence structures, Alexander’s pattern language offers a vocabulary from which an almost infinite number of combinations can emerge.

Writers also draw upon patterns that give a story its coherence. The intimate language between lovers and friends is different from the language used in public. A gesture repeated at different moments. An object that acquires new meaning each time it appears. A place to which a character returns, changed by what has happened in the intervening years.

Like the patterns Alexander describes, these elements can be deceptively simple. Their power comes from their relationships to one another; from the way they accumulate meaning.

There is something reassuring in Alexander’s belief that places of great beauty and humanity can emerge from patterns of experience accumulated over time. No single element needs to carry the entire weight of the design. The same is true of a novel. Its meaning often resides not in a single dramatic revelation, but in the quiet recurrence of images, gestures, and experiences that gradually form the world of a story.

**Christopher Alexander,[A Timeless Way of Building](https://bookshop.org/a/132/9780195024029)**

In *A Timeless Way of Being,* Alexander attempts to name something that is, by its nature, difficult to articulate– “a quality without a name,” or, the quality that makes a place feel alive. It is not style or fashion, nor is it conventionally beautiful. Alexander speaks of a quality that has fire, something connected to nature, to wholeness, and to impermanence. There is a similar quality in literature. There are novels whose structures are well plotted, whose sentences are beautifully wrought, and yet something essential remains absent. And there are others, perhaps less formally perfect, that seem to breathe. Their characters live in our imaginations long after we’ve closed the book.

What gives a work that mysterious vitality?

Alexander suggests that a building acquires its deepest integrity when it emerges from a process attentive to its surroundings, materials, history, and the people who have or will inhabit it. Rather than imposing a predetermined form, the architect must learn to recognize what the place itself is asking for.

In writing, we begin with an idea, perhaps even a carefully imagined structure, but at some point, the work makes demands of its own. Characters can resist, making it essential to shift the original idea. There is surrender involved, a willingness to relinquish control and trust what is emerging. The writer, like the architect, must learn when to impose a structure and when to listen if they are to write something with that “quality without a name.”

**Stewart Brand, [How Buildings Learn](https://bookshop.org/a/132/9780140139969)**

Stewart Brand begins with a simple but radical idea: a building is never finished.

We tend to think of architecture as something completed at a particular moment, when the scaffolding comes down, the architect leaves, and the occupants move in. Brand asks us to think of buildings not as static objects but as evolving structures, shaped by the passage of time and the changing needs of their inhabitants.

I find the idea both practical and poetic.

We often think of a story as something that moves from a beginning toward an end, where all the loose ends are neatly tied up. Life rarely works that way, and the lives within a story are never truly finished. Each has a life that preceded the first page and a future that extends beyond the last. What the writer chooses to include or leave out is all part of the craft of storytelling.

Brand’s book suggests that endurance depends not on resisting change, but on making room for it. This is a particularly rich idea for fiction, where the past is never entirely past, and where transformation rarely means beginning again from nothing.

**Clare Cooper Marcus, [House as a Mirror of Self](https://bookshop.org/a/132/9780892541249)**

Clare Cooper Marcus takes the idea of the house as a container for memory and extends it into psychology. Drawing on Jungian thought and interviews with people about their homes, she explores the possibility that the places we create around ourselves are, in some ways, unconscious portraits of who we are.

For a writer, this is an especially fertile idea. A character’s home can reveal the space between who she believes herself to be and who she actually is. A carefully ordered room may conceal a chaotic inner life. An inherited piece of furniture may carry the weight of an unresolved relationship. A house filled with beautiful things may be a place of profound loneliness. The physical environment becomes a form of characterization, an outward expression of an interior life. And how much of what we build around ourselves is an attempt to recover something lost? How much is an effort to become someone new? Marcus reminds us that the places we inhabit are never psychologically neutral. They are active players in the stories we tell about ourselves, and sometimes they reveal the stories we would rather not tell.

**Ada Louise Huxtable, [On Architecture: Collected Reflections on a Century of Change](https://bookshop.org/a/132/9780802777607)**

Ada Louise Huxtable was a critic—sharp, exacting, and often unsparing—but beneath her judgments was a deep belief in the responsibility of architecture to human beings. She understood that buildings are not simply aesthetic objects. They shape the lives of the people who encounter them, sometimes in ways that are barely perceptible. They influence how we move through cities, how we experience public space, how we understand our place in a community. What I admire about her is her insistence that architecture matters beyond the intentions of its creators. A building exists in the world. It has consequences. It can enlarge our sense of possibility or diminish it. It can offer dignity, beauty, and belonging, or it can disregard the people it is meant to serve.

There is a corresponding responsibility in storytelling. A writer creates a world and invites readers to inhabit that world. The choices a writer makes—whose lives are represented, whose experiences are overlooked, what is revealed and what remains hidden—shape the reader’s encounter with that world and their experience of it. Huxtable’s criticism reminds me that form and beauty are not ends in themselves. A beautifully designed building that doesn’t serve the people who live and work within it, fundamentally doesn’t serve architecture. A story, however purposefully crafted, must also serve the reader beyond just telling a story. Its larger purpose is to lead the reader back into the self, to ignite a resonance of heart and mind.

title: Trotz hoher Belastung: Kita-Fachkräfte sind mit ihrem Beruf überraschend zufrieden
subtitle: Personalmangel, Zeitdruck und hohe Anforderungen prägen den Alltag vieler Kindertageseinrichtungen.
